Cheeky Malware Linked To Popular Gacha Game Cracks City Security

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (609 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • East Asia--and particularly Japan--has been suffering a rash of cybersecurity incidents as of late, affecting everything from major banks and cellphone service providers to city governments and small businesses.
  • Sources indicate that east Asia--and particularly Japan--has been suffering a rash of cybersecurity incidents as of late, affecting everything from major banks and cellphone service providers to city governments and small businesses.
  • One recent incident involved the PC launcher for the popular gacha action shooter NIKKE: Goddess of Victory, where malicious code would install a trojan called k2f that would compromise an individual's PC, taking screenshots, logging inputs, and installing/executing programs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

East Asia--and particularly Japan--has been suffering a rash of cybersecurity incidents as of late, affecting everything from major banks and cellphone service providers to city governments and small businesses. Gaming has been one of many areas targeted: between arcade games on Sega's network going offline, 11 million Capcom IDs being compromised, and a high-schooler hacking Bandai-Namco, some major publishers have been suffering a string of embarrassments. One recent incident involved the PC launcher for the popular gacha action shooter NIKKE: Goddess of Victory, where malicious code would install a trojan called k2f that would compromise an individual's PC, taking screenshots, logging inputs, and installing/executing programs. Unfortunately for one Japanese municipality, someone's gacha habits may have lead to a much bigger incident. Iwamizawa is a city of about 75,000 located in Hokkaido, Japan's northernmost island. It's not a place that makes a lot of news, but it recently went viral on the Japanese-speaking side of social media. As reported by Automaton, the city issued a notice that an IT sub-sub-contractor handling the city's fixed asset records suffered a security breach--specifically, a k2f hijack. Observers soon surmised that the most likely source of k2f would be someone playing a certain sexy gacha game on a work PC. The subcontractor in question, IT services company GIS Hokkaido, would then confirm to Japanese tech news site ITMedia that, yes, NIKKE's compromised PC launcher was the source of the problem. When asked if an employee or subcontractor had launched the game on a work PC, GIS politely replied that "they would prefer not to comment." Moral of the story? While there's nothing wrong with playing a suggestive gacha game on your own time, you probably shouldn't do it on the clock, and definitely not on a company PC, lest you become internet meme fodder.

Latest Update: Wait, How Many People Left Can Actually Win Survivor 51?

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1103 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cinemablend

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that I’m not sure if you’ve noticed, but Survivor 51 is running out of main characters.
  • Jeff Probst has remarked in the past that there’s no one size fits all winner’s edit on Survivor.
  • I’m not saying the person who wins every season is the person with the most confessionals or the person with the most sympathetic edit, but one recurring theme is that the winner is always a consistent and active part of the narrative.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that I’m not sure if you’ve noticed, but Survivor 51 is running out of main characters. We’ve somehow lost four of the biggest, loudest and most vibrant personalities in consecutive weeks, and now, we’re suddenly left with a season that has a few main characters, a couple wacky side characters and a bunch of people who have been consistently deprioritized and underedited throughout the season. What is going on? How many of these castaways can actually even win?

Jeff Probst has remarked in the past that there’s no one size fits all winner’s edit on Survivor. That’s both true and misleading. The longtime host and showrunner is correct in that the winner gets a different story based on their personality and what happened out there (the underdog, the challenge beast, the social threat, etc), but there is one very consistent pattern we do see: screentime.

I’m not saying the person who wins every season is the person with the most confessionals or the person with the most sympathetic edit, but one recurring theme is that the winner is always a consistent and active part of the narrative. The show goes out of their way to give us their perspective on what’s going on because the ultimate payoff needs to feel earned and it needs to make sense. That’s just storytelling 101. If we want to know, for example, why someone on the jury does or doesn’t vote for them at the end, it helps if we’re given context and confessionals about their relationship.

Sources indicate that unfortunately, with nine players left in Survivor 51, there are a ton of players who just aren’t present enough in the edit to seem like viable winners. Seriously, let’s run them down real quick. Cristian has been a little more prominent lately, but he had two confessionals during the first four episodes combined. Despite allegedly being so close to Sharonda that he told her about Carter’s idol, we haven’t seen that relationship developed in the slightest. This season would make no sense if he won.

According to recent reports, it also wouldn’t make any sense if Thien An won. She’s in last place in total confessionals amongst the players left by an absolute mile. Why? I have no idea. She seems to have great social relationships and is an engaging and sometimes cutting confessionalist when she does get a chance to speak, but she’s the least present character in many episodes for unclear reasons. Why would they do that if she won?

Mike and Eric have been much more present parts of the edit, but their storylines have both been about how much everyone else is annoyed with them. Eric has been getting a wacky theater kid edit that has included multiple montages of him talking and everyone else being annoyed by it. There have maybe been ten shots of characters literally rolling their eyes after he talks. Mike is a different version of the same situation. He’s been the subject of numerous confessionals from other players about how he’s a “bottom feeder” and impossible to work with. I don’t see why Survivor would portray its winner that way.

That’s four of the remaining nine players who have seemingly no chance, and I’m not sure Maggie is in a good spot either. She seems to be one of the most well-liked and dangerous players on the entire island. No one would vote for Mike during the Duos Challenge because he was paired with her, and Jelly has dropped confessionals about how she can win if she gets to the end. But the edit also gave her very little credit for Linnea, even though it was her initiative, and she has just over half as many confessionals as Jelly does (24 to 46).

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

That leaves literally four players: Jelly, Devin, Sharonda and Carter. I’d normally write Carter off because he has two episodes with zero confessionals and no player since Survivor 41 has won with even a single zero confessional episode, but as you can see, we’re a little short on viable winner possibilities. I’m out here trying to make excuses for people’s edits and see some silver lining showing why they could win. I think Carter can win. He’s at least been pretty present during the majority of the season. We’ve gotten his viewpoint consistently, and we’ve gotten confessionals from other people that speak of him very highly.

So, yeah, Carter is a maybe, but really, that leaves us with Jelly, Devin and Sharonda. The Helicopter Alliance has been the most consistent narrative throughline of the entire season, which is why it makes sense that these three are at the top of the list. Jelly and Devin have, without question, been the main characters of 52 (at least since Brady left), and they’re dominating in screentime and confessionals at 46 and 45 respectively. That’s twelve more than Eric, who is in third place of those remaining thanks to a bunch of vampire analogies and references to his fiance Gina.

Sharonda is quite a bit behind with 29 confessionals. Like Carter, there are some concerns with her edit, as there have been stretches where she hasn’t been super prominent, but her content has been so overwhelmingly positive that I’m willing to give her a pass. I still consider her a very viable winner at this point, as she should come into further prominence in the edit once the other players find out she’s been secretly working with Devin and Jelly the entire time.

I don’t know who is going to win Survivor 52. There are three, maybe four viable candidates with Maggie and maybe Mike added in there as wild longshots. That’s a really small number of people in play for there being nine castaways left. In fact, it’s starting to feel a little like Survivor 49 where the entire fanbase was convinced one member of the Tres Leches alliance was going to win because they were the only people who seemed viable for like the entire second half of the game (apart from maybe Steven I guess).

Industry observers note that lack of winning edits aside and a few questionable twist-related decisions aside, Survivor 51 has been an absolute banger so far. Fingers crossed it’s able to stick the landing and fulfill its potential to be an all-time great season, whether one of these obvious contenders wins or not.

  • In a recent development, the AirPods Max 2, which introduced in March, are already down to $449.99 from $549, saving you nearly $100 on Apple's premium over-ear headphones.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Amazon's early Black Friday sale is bringing some pretty significant discounts on Apple devices, including several of the company's latest releases. The biggest savings are on the M5 MacBook Air, with up to $249 off, though there are plenty of smaller deals worth considering, too, from the AirPods Pro 3 at $179.00 to the Apple Pencil Pro at $99. You'll also find discounts on iPads, the Mac mini, and everyday accessories like the Magic Keyboard, Magic Trackpad, and AirTags. With Apple raising prices across its Mac and iPad lineups in June, citing higher memory chip costs, these sales offer a good opportunity to upgrade without paying full price.

The AirPods Pro 3 are down to $179 from $249, saving you $70 on Apple's latest premium wireless earbuds. They offer improved active noise cancellation over the previous generation, along with redesigned foam-infused ear tips and a heart-rate sensor that tracks workouts without an Apple Watch. They also support Live Translation with a compatible iPhone and carry an IP57 rating for sweat and water resistance. PCMag’s review goes into more detail on how they perform.

In a recent development, the AirPods Max 2, which introduced in March, are already down to $449.99 from $549, saving you nearly $100 on Apple's premium over-ear headphones. The biggest upgrade over the original model is the H2 chip, which Apple says makes active noise cancellation up to 1.5 times more effective while introducing features like Adaptive Audio, Conversation Awareness, and Live Translation. For more on its performance, check out this PCMag review.

Industry observers note that the Apple Watch Series 12 (GPS, 42mm) is down to $329 from $399, saving you $70. It covers everything you'd expect from a premium smartwatch, including fitness tracking, health monitoring, notifications, and the ability to take calls when your iPhone is nearby. PCMag gave it an "outstanding" rating in its review and also named it its Gift of the Year for 2026.

If you'd prefer to occasionally leave your iPhone behind, the Apple Watch Series 12 (GPS + Cellular, 42mm) is $70 off, bringing its price down to $429 from $499. It has all the same features as the GPS model but adds cellular connectivity, allowing you to make calls, send messages, and stream music even when your phone isn't nearby (provided you have an active cellular plan).

For a more affordable option, the Apple Watch SE 3 (GPS, 40mm) is down to $199 from $249, saving you $50. It covers the essentials, including workout tracking, daily activity monitoring, and notifications, making it a practical choice if you don't need the Series 12's more advanced health features. Check out PCMag's review for a closer look at what you get for the price.

According to recent reports, the Apple Watch SE 3 (GPS + Cellular, 40mm) is also $50 off, bringing its price down to $249 from $299. For an extra $50 over the GPS-only model, you get the convenience of making calls, sending messages, and staying connected without keeping your iPhone nearby, provided you have an active cellular plan. It's worth considering if you regularly go for runs, head to the gym, or step out without your phone but still want to stay reachable.

It has been revealed that apple released the M5 MacBook Air in March with 512GB of base storage, double the previous generation's, along with a faster SSD and an N1 wireless chip that adds Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6. Right now, the 15-inch M5 MacBook Air (512GB) is down to $1,249.99 from $1,499. For a closer look at the M5 MacBook Air's performance and features, check out PCMag's review.

If you prefer a more compact laptop but need extra storage, the 13-inch M5 MacBook Air with a 1TB SSD is down to $1,399.99 from $1,599, saving you $200. That's twice the storage of the base model, giving you more room for large files, photos, videos, and applications without having to rely as heavily on external drives or cloud storage. You still get the M5 chip, faster SSD performance, and Wi-Fi 7 support, all in a smaller, lighter design.

The M6 Mac mini is down to $949.99 from $1,099, saving you $149 on Apple's latest compact desktop. Its 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU can handle everything from everyday multitasking to photo editing and more demanding creative work, while the upgraded Neural Engine helps with AI-related tasks—Apple says the M6 delivers substantial performance improvements over the earlier M4 model, particularly for graphics and AI workloads. For more on how it performs in everyday use, check out PCMag's review.

The M4 iPad Air launched in March, and the 13-inch model is already down to $949.99 from $1,049, saving you nearly $100. Its M4 chip can comfortably handle demanding tasks like photo editing, digital illustration, and multitasking, while the 13-inch Liquid Retina display gives you plenty of room to work across apps. You also get 256GB of storage for your files and creative projects. For more on what to expect, here's PCMag's review.

If you need more storage for your creative projects, the 13-inch M4 iPad Air with 512GB is $100 off, bringing its price down to $1,149 from $1,249. That's double the storage of the 256GB model, giving you more room for large photo libraries, video projects, downloaded files, and apps without having to rely as heavily on cloud storage.

For those looking for something more powerful, the 11-inch iPad Pro with the M5 chip and 512GB of storage is down to $1,299.99 from $1,399, saving you nearly $100. Along with the faster processor, it offers an Ultra Retina XDR OLED display with ProMotion support for refresh rates up to 120Hz, making it particularly well-suited for creative work, video editing, and other demanding tasks.

The Apple Magic Keyboard with Numeric Keypad is down to $109 from $129, saving you $20 on a wireless keyboard designed primarily for Mac users. It pairs wirelessly over Bluetooth and can be recharged using USB-C. For a closer look at all that it has to offer, check out PCMag's review.

The Magic Trackpad is down to $130 from $149, taking $19 off an accessory that brings the Multi-Touch gestures and Force Touch pressure sensing of a MacBook trackpad to a desktop setup, across an edge-to-edge glass surface. It connects wirelessly over Bluetooth and has a rechargeable battery that lasts about a month between charges. You can read PCMag's full review to see how it stacks up.

According to recent reports, the Apple Pencil Pro is down to $99 from $129, saving you $30 on Apple's most feature-rich stylus. It adds squeeze and barrel-roll gestures, haptic feedback, and Find My support to Apple's stylus lineup, and it pairs and charges magnetically along the side of a compatible iPad, including the M4 iPad Air featured above. For more on its strengths and limitations, check out PCMag's review.

According to recent reports, the second-generation AirTag, released in January, keeps the original's size so existing holders still fit, while a new Ultra Wideband chip extends Precision Finding range by up to 50% and a redesigned speaker plays 50% louder. Right now, its four-pack is down to $79.99 from $99.99, which works out to $20 per tag, compared with $29 for a single AirTag. PCMag's review offers a more detailed look at how it holds up in everyday use.

The Apple Magic Mouse is down to $59.99 from $79.99, saving you $20 on Apple's wireless mouse with a Multi-Touch surface that lets you swipe between pages and scroll through documents using simple finger gestures. It connects to your Mac over Bluetooth and has a rechargeable battery.

Yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

Among the deals listed here, the M5 MacBook Air with 512 of storage has one of the larger discounts at $249 off, bringing its price down to $1,249.99, from $1499.

Recent findings suggest that for most people, the Apple Watch SE 3 at $199 is a good starting point, covering everyday fitness tracking, notifications, and essential health features without the higher price of the Series 12. If you want more advanced health monitoring and a more premium smartwatch experience, the Series 12 at $329 is worth considering.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, one of the biggest horror movies of the year, "Obsession," finally landed on Netflix this week, where Inde Navarrette's unhinged performance will no doubt haunt even more people's nightmares. If you’re still reeling from its tense atmosphere and wonder what other horror movies on Netflix capture that same sense of creeping dread and paranoia, I've got you covered.

I watch a lot of horror movies, and my top three picks for what to watch after "Obsession" are sure to fit the vibe you're looking for. Two of them come from acclaimed horror series director Mike Flanagan, while the third is a slept-on horror mystery thriller with a perfect 100% score on Rotten Tomatoes that flips the haunted house trope on its head.

So without further ado, let's dive into the best horror movies on Netflix to watch after "Obsession.".

Just like "Obsession," "Hush" is another example of a simple premise executed well. It's also helmed by Mike Flanagan before he established himself as the king of TV horror with "The Haunting of Hill House," "Midnight Mass" and "Carrie." This slasher movie stars Flanagan's wife and long-time collaborator Kate Siegel as Maddie, a deaf and mute woman who becomes the target of a masked killer.

It's lean, tightly wound horror movie that wrings a surprising amount of tension from its simple premise. The isolated setting of a house in the remote woods also adds to the atmosphere of constant unease, like you're being watched. And while Maddie is relentlessly stalked and tormented by the killer, she's never reduced to a helpless victim, which makes this one of the more empowering genre entries.

With remarkable direction from Remi Weekes (who also wrote the screenplay), strong performances from the whole cast ("Doctor Who’s" Matt Smith has a small role) and plenty of terrifying moments, "His House" is a certified chiller — and one of the best Netflix horror movies. Whenever I recommend essential horror movies to get non-horror fans into the genre, "His House" tops the list.

Industry observers note that "His House" follows a young refugee couple, Bol (Sope Dirisu) and Rial (Wunmi Mosaku), who are granted asylum in a small English town after fleeing war-torn South Sudan. They struggle to adjust, and straining their relationship further is the supernatural terror haunting their home that seems connected to their past. But while Rial insists something is not right and wants to move, Bol worries that making waves could get them deported. And so the two are left on their own to face whatever's haunting them.

Watch "His House" on Netflix now.

Another one from Flanagan (can you tell I'm a fan?), this trippy horror movie adds a fresh perspective to a familiar framework, where a cursed mirror not only warps the minds of the main characters, but leaves the audience questioning what's real and what's a hallucination. Noted mirror is responsible for the deaths of Kaylie (Karen Gillan) and Tim's (Brenton Thwaites) parents, who began acting strange and talking to the apparition of a dark-haired woman (Siegel) before they passed.

Industry observers note that adding to this disorientation, "Oculus" shift between two timelines: when the siblings were young and first witnessing the mirror's horrible influence, and then 11 years later when they come back to put an end to its demented reign of terror for good. Gillan gives a gloriously unhinged performance as her obsession (haha, get it?) with finally proving the mirror's curse is real ends up being her downfall when her carefully laid looks start falling apart.

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1081 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • From Kate unexpectedly presenting an award and delivering a speech at the star-studded Earthshot Prize event to her and William playing cricket and traveling around Mumbai in an electric rickshaw, there have been plenty of photo opportunities and headlines around the world about the environmental initiative William is so passionate about.
  • According to royals author Russell Myers, who followed the couple on tour, the speech Kate gave at the awards was kept top secret.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Prince William and Kate Middleton’s visit to India for the Earthshot Prize ceremony marked their first joint overseas tour in four years, and the couple used it as an opportunity to demonstrate their star power. Through their action-packed itinerary, which took them from Mumbai to Fresh Delhi, the Prince and Princess of Wales have paved the way for a new style of royal tour.

From Kate unexpectedly presenting an award and delivering a speech at the star-studded Earthshot Prize event to her and William playing cricket and traveling around Mumbai in an electric rickshaw, there have been plenty of photo opportunities and headlines around the world about the environmental initiative William is so passionate about.

According to royals author Russell Myers, who followed the couple on tour, the speech Kate gave at the awards was kept top secret. “None of us knew she was presenting an award on the night, or that she was going to speak. The auditorium was packed. There were about 5,000 people there. It’s been the biggest Earthshot yet, and you could see Catherine was nervous, but she delivered an absolutely brilliant speech. I’d say her best yet.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s been wonderful for her to be here, supporting William, and you can see they’ve really had fun. Because of ongoing terror threats, there have been less walkabouts, but it’s been a very successful and varied tour, and I think, being shorter than most tours, it sets a fresh blueprint when it comes to royal tours for the couple in the future.”.

Prince William and Princess Kate arrive to attend the Earthshot Prize awards night at the Jio World Convention Centre on November 17, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

There are seemingly already intends for another royal tour, notes Myers.

“William let slip that Australia is on the cards next, and if that’s the case, I imagine they will go as a family. They don’t want to be away from their children for too long, and what a way it would be to win support for the monarchy Down Under,” Myers says.

Sources indicate that according to royals insiders, there had been some nervousness around the trip after the couple’s disastrous tour of the Caribbean in March 2022, when their visit was overshadowed by calls for the UK to apologize for slavery. Then some of their photo calls, including one that involved the couple riding in an open-top Land Rover, led to accusations of the royals appearing colonial and out of touch.

According to recent reports, “I think there has been a slight nervousness about how this tour would be received, but the reception has been really good,” Myers notes. “The fact that William and Catherine have included a visit to Upcoming Delhi to see Prime Minister Modi is a clever move. While this is a private trip to promote Earthshot, the Foreign Office was keen for William to meet with the Indian prime minister, so they have packed that into the itinerary too.”.

Recent findings suggest that the visit to India has come at a time when the royals are on something of a charm offensive following a difficult year for the royal family, from Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor’s arrest to what one palace insider calls “the ongoing soap opera” with Prince Harry and Meghan Markle. (Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor has not been charged and has denied all allegations of wrongdoing.).

William and Kate are keen to carve out their own initiatives and projects focusing on their major priorities, including the environment, children’s early years, and mental health. With the challenge of having Harry and Meghan carrying out their own engagements, the Prince and Princess of Wales have been careful to establish clear parameters that set them apart as working royals. In one telling moment while on an engagement in Mumbai, Kate was asked for an autograph. She politely declined, so as not to breach protocol, a clear contrast to the Duchess of Sussex, who has signed autographs in the past.

“Catherine was asked to sign an autograph, but she was right not to. It wasn’t a snub; it was just adhering to protocol. An autograph could be sold for money,” notes Dickie Arbiter, former press secretary to Queen Elizabeth II.

According to author Tom Bower, the royals are more relatable now than they were during the reign of Queen Elizabeth II, who famously never gave a press interview. In recent weeks, Prince William has appeared as a guest on The Graham Norton Show (to promote Earthshot), and he’s revealed how he drinks his cider and his love of wild swimming as part of his guest-editing stint for a recent issue of Country Life magazine.

“The royals are more relatable, perhaps, than they ever have been, but they are not celebrities. There’s a danger of being too relatable, too much ‘one of the people,’ which means they can lose some of their mystery,” Bower says.

According to recent reports, “William will have been advised to do TV appearances and take on media opportunities to bolster his public image. Of course, it’s charming to hear these nuggets and see this side of the prince, but I do think there’s a need to see and hear more from William about his broader plans. Over the years, Charles has made huge efforts to appeal to all cultural aspects of society. I’m not sure William has done that. He’s got to find a way of connecting with everyone, not just the younger generation,” Bower adds.

The Earthshot Prize awards have been a powerful way of demonstrating that William doesn’t just talk the talk; he is insisting on action.

Sources indicate that “The Earthshot is a master class in what needs to be done,” concludes Arbiter. “He’s pushing for environmental problems and climate change, and he’s getting people to do something about it. The fact that he is so well supported, and by so many high-profile people, demonstrates his pulling power and influence.”.

Why iPhone Duo wasn’t for me (but might be for you)

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (839 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I’ve had the iPhone Duo for nearly two weeks now, and have officially decided to return it.
  • I use my iPhone one-handed all the time, and based on my experience, iPhone Duo is clearly intended to be used with two hands.
  • It has been revealed that perhaps over time I’d get used to needing two hands for most iPhone interactions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I’ve had the iPhone Duo for nearly two weeks now, and have officially decided to return it. Here are the three main reasons why the Duo didn’t work out for me, but might for you.

I use my iPhone one-handed all the time, and based on my experience, iPhone Duo is clearly intended to be used with two hands. You can use it one-handed, but for me it’s not nearly as comfortable as the iPhone 18 Pro. It’s too wide and too heavy to be used for long.

It has been revealed that perhaps over time I’d get used to needing two hands for most iPhone interactions. But that would be a pretty significant shift for me, as there are so many situations when I don’t have both hands free.

Sources indicate that if you already use two hands with your iPhone regularly—perhaps because you have a Pro Max model—then the Duo’s one-handed experience likely won’t bother you. But the more I used the Duo, the more I found myself missing my iPhone 18 Pro.

The biggest value proposition of a foldable is that it’s a 2-in-1 product, letting you have a standard phone but also a tablet-sized display that fits in your pocket.

Sources indicate that I totally get the appeal, and fully expected to love that hybrid design. But after two weeks of trying, I still struggled to find times when I actually wanted to unfold the Duo. And to be clear, that’s a me problem, not an problem with the Duo itself.

I tried a bunch of apps on the inner display, and struggled to find use cases that—for me—made it worthwhile to open the Duo. But based on the feedback I’ve seen from most Duo owners, I’m very much in the minority.

It has been revealed that I know lots of people love the Duo for video, but I don’t watch much video on my iPhone. I almost never watch YouTube, TikTok, or Instagram Reels. And for highlights and movies, I stick with my TV screen and an Apple TV 4K.

Multitasking support on iPhone Duo works really well. But when I found myself needing to multitask, I still reached for my iPad Pro with Magic Keyboard attached. A keyboard-free product can’t replace my main computer (nor would I expect it to), and the Duo screen was too small to comfortably work on it.

Last year I bought an iPhone Air and absolutely loved it. Initially, the Air’s less capable camera system didn’t bother me, it was “good enough.”.

After a few months though, I started missing the Pro camera system more. Then I learned that my wife was pregnant with twins, and I knew I wanted the best possible iPhone cameras to capture their early weeks and months. So I bought an iPhone 18 Pro in September.

In a recent development, I’ve been very impressed by iPhone 18 Pro’s Main camera upgrades, and it’s great having a Telephoto lens again too. Since having the best camera system is so crucial for me right now, I knew iPhone Duo couldn’t be my only iPhone.

According to recent reports, I initially planned to dual-carry the two models, using iPhone 18 Pro solely as a camera. But over and over I found myself wishing it was my only iPhone.

Sources indicate that I returned mine as well. Beautiful device, but functionally not very good.

Is the iPhone Duo camera good enough for most people? Probably so. But for this year at least, with my twins aging rapidly, it’s not quite right for me. If I loved the Duo for other reasons, I would just use both models. But since I didn’t, I’m happy to stick with the iPhone 18 Pro.

In closing, I want to explicitly state that I don’t think the iPhone Duo is a bad product, and this isn’t a “bad review.”.

The iPhone Duo just isn’t for me. I get the sense, though, that it’s lots of people’s favorite iPhone in years. Apple created its most unique fresh iPhone model since the original, and there’s plenty to love about it. I’m very curious to see how popular foldables become over time compared to slab models, because each clearly offers pros and cons. But for me, at least right now, the iPhone 18 Pro is my model of choice.

Sources indicate that what has your iPhone Duo experience been like so far? Love it? Undecided? Let us know in the comments.

10 Shows Like 'MobLand' You Should Watch Next

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Crime dramas often attract big stars, and MobLand is no exception.
  • Sources indicate that while families are complicated in even the best of circumstances, that's especially true of the Family.
  • Recent findings suggest that theo James plays army officer Eddie Horniman (a name mentioned as often as possible), heir to the Horniman estate (there it is again) who, upon the death of his father, is named the Duke of Halstead.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Crime dramas often attract big stars, and MobLand is no exception. The Paramount+ series stars Tom Hardy as mob fixer Harry Da Souza, with Pierce Brosnan and Paddy Considine in supporting roles and Helen Mirren having a ball as the thoroughly evil matriarch of the Harrigan crime family.

Sources indicate that while families are complicated in even the best of circumstances, that's especially true of the Family. After you've watched the recently released second season of MobLand, try one of these other demonstrates mixing crime and family (or Family) drama.

Recent findings suggest that theo James plays army officer Eddie Horniman (a name mentioned as often as possible), heir to the Horniman estate (there it is again) who, upon the death of his father, is named the Duke of Halstead. He learns that his dad was tied to various criminal enterprises, and that his scouse brother is millions of pounds in debt to a drug dealer. What else is the dapper, military-trained Duke to do but learn to navigate the violent underworld while looking cool? You won't be surprised to learn that this British crime drama comes from creator/writer/producer Guy Ritchie, who also has a hand in MobLand. Stream The Gentlemen on Netflix.

Another series from Taylor Sheridan (the Yellowstone guy), this pandemic-era hit stars Jeremy Renner as Mike McLusky, head of a family that’s been keeping the peace, through means fair and foul, in the title's firm town for decades. The "business" of the corrupt burg happens to be incarceration, and the McLuskys thrive when business is up, even if Mike has slightly different ideas about how to run things. The show deals broadly with systemic racism and inequality in the prison system, but mostly it's a modern-day western about bringing justice to a corrupt town. It will conclude with a fifth season, streaming in 2027. Stream Mayor of Kingstown on Paramount+.

A consistently compelling combination of smart plotting and lurid sex and violence, Banshee stars Antony Starr as Sheriff Lucas Hood...kinda: He's actually a man recently released from prison who takes over that identity when the new sheriff in the small town of Banshee is killed before anyone really has a chance to get to know him. It's all part of a complicated strategy to reunite with his lover Ana (Ivana Miličević), and to get back the $15 million in diamonds he lost when he went to jail—but the town is ruled over by various criminal factions, and being sheriff doesn't guarantee any kind of safety; rather, the opposite. Stream Banshee on HBO Max.

In a recent development, mobLand creator Ronan Bennett previously made this acclaimed series that succeeds by maintaining a narrow scope—in this case, a single London council estate. Dushane (Ashley Walters) and Sully (Kane Robinson) are residents and drug dealers at Summerhouse, maintaining an increasingly precarious grip on the criminal element in the community. Most compellingly, the series maintains an extensive supporting cast of locals both in the drug trade and impacted by it, building a disturbingly compelling world. A little confusingly, the first couple of seasons were renamed Top Boy: Summerhouse when the show moved to Netflix, so you'll want to start there before moving on to plain ol' Top Boy. Stream Top Boy: Summerhouse on Netflix.

Sources indicate that based loosely on a nonfiction work investigating the Mafia-like Camorra in Campania, this show focuses on the head of the Savastano clan, Pietro Savastano (Fortunato Cerlino), and his ambitious lieutenant Ciro Di Marzio (Marco D'Amore). When Pietro is arrested at the series' outset, a civil war erupts between family members and among the factions vying for control. Gone are the suits and poker games of many a mob drama—this is a brutal, street-level take on organized crime that forsakes the typical trappings of the genre. Stream Gomorrah on HBO Max.

I'm here for the Pierce Brosnan of it all, but there's also a very strong vibe match in this series that casts the one-time James Bond actor as the head of a literal crime family, even if this one's set in the American West. Adapting Philipp Meyer's 2013 Pulitzer Prize-nominated novel of the same name, the series follows Eli McCullough, a ruthless cattle baron making moves to get in on the burgeoning oil industry in the Rio Grande Valley of 1915. A parallel narrative sees Eli as a young man, kidnapped and raised among a Nʉmʉnʉʉ family. While his backstory lends the character welcome complexity, in the present, he's as determined to build his empire as he is to prepare his son and grandson to take over when he's gone. Stream The Son on Prime Video.

Tom Hardy playing a tough guy isn't terribly unexpected, but here the setting is London, just after the end of the War of 1812. Hardy plays James Delaney, who returns from Africa after ten years away (he says he'd been taken prisoner, but his story doesn't entirely add up) for the funeral of his father. Dad left nothing but a little hunk of land off of Vancouver, not worth much until the war's conclusion creates new maritime trade opportunities. Suddenly, the United States, Great Britain, and the East India Company all have eyes on the real estate, and all are willing to do whatever it takes to acquire it—and the stakes become clear once James realizes that his father's cause of death wasn't natural. Stream Taboo on Peacock and Tubi.

Best not ponder too much on the fact that this one's based on a video game, as its pedigree is only hinted at via the levels of action and violence (certainly compared to some of the other indicates on this list). Colm Meaney plays Finn Wallace, the absolutely indispensable leader of London's criminal underworld, a man who's been holding everything together for decades, until his shocking murder at the outset of the series (that's not a spoiler, and we spend more time with him via flashbacks). The completely random killing by someone who had no idea what he was doing begets chaos and open violence. Finn's son Sean (Joe Cole) has been raised to take his father's place, but local, Pakistani, and Albanian gangs all move in to take control from the Finn family in the power vacuum. Stream Gangs of London on AMC+.

Sources indicate that the great Forest Whitaker stars as the real-life Bumpy Johnson, who returned from a prison sentence to find his neighborhood falling apart and in the grip of Italian mobsters. A more than capable crime boss in his own right, Johnson resolves to take on the Genovese crime family, eventually forming a tentative alliance with Malcolm X (Nigél Thatch and, later, Jason Alan Carvell). Johnson is the lesser evil as far as Malcolm and others are concerned, and a complicated figure as both crime lord and family man with aspirations of saving his neighborhood. The show will conclude with a two-hour finale, likely airing in 2027. Stream Godfather of Harlem on Hulu.

Adopted into an Italian organized crime family as a baby, Park Joo-hyung took on the name Vincenzo Cassano, eventually becoming a mafia consigliere. After his adoptive father Don Fabio dies, Fabio’s biological son comes gunning for his brother, whom he now sees as competition. Cassano flees to Seoul, on the hunt for a secret stash of money, and in the process discovers a love interest and a upcoming adversary in a giant business conglomerate that definitely deserves to be taken down. An incredibly popular K-drama, this one definitely puts a unique spin on the tropes of the mob genre. Stream Vincenzo on Netflix.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that for those curious but still want to watch for themselves, I'll keep this spoiler-free.
  • Industry observers note that project Hail Mary was called "blatant Catholic propaganda," as described by someone who never watched, and similarly, The Body is being vilified by groups of concerned Catholics who have not and likely will not watch it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the Body is available to stream right now with a Netflix subscription, and when I learned it was about controversy surrounding a Catholic school, I had to check it out. As someone who attended a Catholic grade school and high school, I was eager to see how it was portrayed, and while things were a bit wilder than I remember, the show really nailed two parts.

It has been revealed that for those curious but still want to watch for themselves, I'll keep this spoiler-free. All readers really need to know going in is that this series surrounds a Catholic school dance team, and what happens when an initiation prank goes too far and a student's life is in danger.

Industry observers note that project Hail Mary was called "blatant Catholic propaganda," as described by someone who never watched, and similarly, The Body is being vilified by groups of concerned Catholics who have not and likely will not watch it. As someone who did, I'll admit no one should go into this assuming it'll be a family-friendly adventure, but the parts that handle religion are done with lots of care.

I say this, especially, as a person who went through their teenage years in Catholic school. For many, your teens are going to be one of the most rebellious and potentially dangerous times of your lives. Imagine some of the wildest things you did in high school, and now imagine the feeling that you'll be eternally damned for it days afterward.

Industry observers note that "Catholic Guilt," they call it, is shown in full effect in The Body. Obviously, there are people in this who deserve to feel guilty, but there are also cases in which we see characters feel immense guilt or shame for things that would otherwise be quite normal today.

In a recent development, some of this is due to The Body being set in 2004, when things like LGBTQ+ relationships weren't as prevalent in pop culture and were largely frowned upon in Catholic schools. Pregnant teens at my high school weren't allowed to walk to get their diploma at graduation, and I couldn't imagine what would happen if someone were openly gay back then.

According to recent reports, and yet these things happened, and these people existed. It's one of the things I love about The Body, and the way it navigates what would undoubtedly be a scary time for those individuals. Again, it was more extreme than anything I dealt with, but I know that feeling of guilt quite well.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

I also think The Body does a great job of handling what goes down when something controversial does happen at a Catholic school. I can't get into specifics, but there was a controversy at my school so major that it received national attention, and the fact that it was a Catholic school only amplified the interest and headlines.

The Internet Can’t Stop Talking About People’s Mouths In Netflix’s The Christmas Switch. I Can’t Unsee It.

It has been revealed that like the kids in The Body, a number of kids attending were from families of some renown. Families were willing to keep quiet about events occurring to protect their children, and the school was eager to let any controversy fade as quickly as possible.

There's certainly something to the added pressure of a Catholic school striving to be perfect. As The Body points out, any controversy draws the same critics who will immediately point to past incidents highlighted by the movie Spotlight. No one wants to be the person to bring added negative attention to the religion, but at the end of the day it's a high school full of rowdy teens just like any other.

It has been revealed that I'm admittedly a lapsed Catholic, but I would say The Body was the best representation in media for the faith since Wake Up, Dead Man. In that, both deal with Catholicism, but not so much that they're openly mocking or blaspheming it. They're stories about the people who practice it, who are imperfect and flawed. I don't think teachers should show it in class, but it is worth a watch for those who are curious.

According to recent reports, check out The Body and other upcoming Netflix shows as 2026 winds down. With the holidays right around the corner, there's nothing like watching something controversial to spark some conversation at the family dinner table!

Sources indicate that airPods got a variety of new features this fall in iOS 27, several of which are exclusive to AirPods Pro 3 (now only $179). Here’s everything new.

Custom EQ is a feature that some AirPods customers thought Apple would never ship, but iOS 27 adds it.

With Custom EQ, Apple now lets you set your own sound profile for AirPods. Per Apple:.

According to recent reports, airPods are designed and engineered by Apple to faithfully represent music, TV shows and movies, and calls. If you prefer a different sound profile, you can customize how AirPods represent any audio played.

In a recent development, you can change the EQ by going to your AirPods’ settings ⇾ Audio & Routing ⇾ Equalizer ⇾ Custom. From here, you can adjust the sound profile for low, mid, and high frequencies.

Custom EQ is available on AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Max 2, AirPods 5, and AirPods 4.

Apple GymKit has been available for years, but only for Apple Watch. It lets you pair and sync workout data with compatible cardio equipment, like treadmills, ellipticals, indoor bikes, and more.

In iOS 27, GymKit expands to support iPhone using AirPods Pro 3’s heart rate sensor. My colleague Zac gave it a try:.

It has been revealed that the setup is simple. I tapped my iPhone to the treadmill, picked Indoor Walk (Indoor Run is also offered), and started the workout from the treadmill. With GymKit, workout data is stored privately on iPhone and removed from the equipment.

It has been revealed that once the workout started, the treadmill received heart-rate data from AirPods Pro 3. Meanwhile, the Fitness app on iPhone received the treadmill’s distance, pace, incline, and calorie data. Treadmills know details that an iPhone and AirPods can’t know on their own, especially incline and precise belt distance.

For more details on iOS 27’s GymKit feature for AirPods Pro 3, check out Zac’s full hands-on below.

Read more: iOS 27 basically turns your iPhone and AirPods into an Apple Watch at the gym.

For most AirPods users, the single biggest upgrade in iOS 27 is Siri AI.

Siri AI is available on compatible iPhone hardware in iOS 27, and Apple made sure to expand full support for the AI assistant to AirPods too.

Industry observers note that airPods are essentially becoming an AI wearable thanks to the newly introduced Siri. It will let consumers do a lot more than the current Siri. Here are some key features via Apple’s website:.

Earlier this year when AirTag 2 debuted, Apple brought Precision Finding support to Apple Watch for the first time. Until now though, it’s been limited to AirTag 2.

But with iOS 27 and watchOS 27, Apple expands Precision Finding on the Watch to AirPods Pro 3.

AirPods Pro 3’s case includes the latest second-generation Ultra Wideband (UWB) chip, letting you find it with greater precision and step-by-step guidance right from your wrist.

With every batch of new AirPods features that debuts, the AirPods settings screen in the Settings app gets more cluttered.

But in iOS 27, Apple has a welcome fix: it’s redesigned and reorganized all AirPods settings.

Now, you’ll find AirPods settings organized into more categories and submenus, accompanied by colorful icons. It makes finding the right setting way easier and more intuitive than before.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, 2026 has been a pretty decent year for new movies so far, but that doesn’t mean we’ve escaped the usual problem of some genuinely entertaining releases slipping under the radar.
  • In a recent development, thankfully, Prime Video has now added “They Will Kill You” to its library, which I’m hoping will give this overlooked gem a chance to find a much bigger audience.
  • In a recent development, in fact, I’d argue it’s one of the more entertaining horror releases of the year so far.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, 2026 has been a pretty decent year for new movies so far, but that doesn’t mean we’ve escaped the usual problem of some genuinely entertaining releases slipping under the radar. One such film is “They Will Kill You,” a gloriously bonkers mash-up of survival, comedy and horror that pits a tough-as-nails woman against a group of seriously unhinged cult members. The whole thing feels like a fever dream, with outrageous violence, ridiculous twists and enough carnage to keep you wondering what on earth you’re watching.

In a recent development, thankfully, Prime Video has now added “They Will Kill You” to its library, which I’m hoping will give this overlooked gem a chance to find a much bigger audience. Its theatrical run certainly didn’t do it any favors, with the movie reportedly earning approximately $19 million worldwide against a production budget of $20 million, making it a box office disappointment. That’s a shame, because while it’s not a perfect film by any means, it’s certainly not a bad one.

In a recent development, in fact, I’d argue it’s one of the more entertaining horror releases of the year so far. It knows exactly how ridiculous it wants to be and has plenty of fun with its increasingly chaotic set pieces. I left the theater genuinely shocked by some of the things I witnessed, but also grinning at just how much fun I'd had. If you missed it on the big screen, its arrival on Prime Video is a pretty good excuse to put that right, and here’s why.

“They Will Kill You” follows Asia Reaves (Zazie Beetz), a young woman who takes a live-in housekeeping job at The Virgil, a luxurious New York City apartment building, hoping to find her missing younger sister, Maria (Myha'la). However, Asia soon discovers that the building’s wealthy residents are hiding a terrifying secret: they’re members of a satanic cult that has been sacrificing unsuspecting workers for decades.

When the residents attempt to make Asia their latest victim, they promptly discover she’s not quite as helpless as they expected. Trapped inside the building with seemingly no way out, Asia must fight her way through its corridors and take on an increasingly dangerous group of attackers. With time running out and Maria caught up in the cult’s plans, Asia faces a brutal fight to get them both out alive.

It has been revealed that I’ll admit, I was a little worried “They Will Kill You” might struggle to stand out, especially arriving shortly after “Ready or Not 2,” which has a pretty similar premise involving two sisters trying to escape a cult. Thankfully, Zazie Beetz gives this film a flavor of its own. She’s an absolute badass, throwing herself into some wonderfully chaotic fight scenes and getting covered in blood more times than I can count. There’s also a noticeably angrier edge to this movie, which I really appreciated. It’s a welcome addition to the horror-comedy genre that isn’t afraid to get properly nasty.

Storytelling isn’t exactly the film’s strong suit, and I wouldn’t say it does anything particularly compelling with its characters or central plot. But that’s not really why I’d recommend it. The real draw is the action, inventive kill scenes and completely unhinged body horror. There are also some wonderfully ridiculous twists involving the cult that had me laughing, while the final act goes so completely off the rails that I was practically squealing (little hint there). It’s an absolute hoot, and I had a ridiculous amount of fun watching it.

It has been revealed that I also really enjoyed the film’s visual style. Director Kirill Sokolov uses graphic compositions that sometimes resemble comic-book panels, alongside unusual framing and some wonderfully eccentric camera angles. There are moments when the whole thing almost feels like you’re watching a video game, particularly during its more elaborate fight sequences. Yes, it’s a little unconventional, but I thought it worked brilliantly with the film’s exaggerated violence and chaotic energy. It gives “They Will Kill You” a distinct visual identity that helps it stand apart from other horror-comedies.

In a recent development, there’s definitely a lack of genuine character connection here, largely because the story doesn’t give you much to work with, but Beetz is such a compelling screen presence that you naturally find yourself rooting for her anyway. She’s more than capable of carrying the film, and I’d happily watch her take on another ridiculous survival scenario. I also think “They Will Kill You” has some serious cult classic potential. It might not have found its audience at the box office back in March, but I wouldn't be surprised if it earns a lot more love in the years ahead as more people discover it. Sometimes all a film needs is a second chance, and this one certainly deserves it.

Stream "They Will Kill You" on Prime Video now.

Sources indicate that alix is a Senior Streaming Writer at Tom’s Guide, which basically means watching the best movies and TV shows and then writing about them. It’s a dream job for someone who’s been obsessed with storytelling since she first figured out how to work a remote.

Before joining Tom’s Guide, Alix honed her skills as a staff writer with outlets like Screen Rant and Bough Digital, where she discovered her love for the entertainment industry.

She heads to the cinema every week as a tradition, no matter what’s showing. For her, movies aren’t just entertainment — they’re a ritual, a comfort, and a constant source of inspiration. When she’s not at her desk or at the cinema, you’ll probably find her deep into a horror video game on her PC.

#62828. This Emerging Artist Is a Hit Restaurateur

📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Vanityfair ↗ Open Full Page

This Emerging Artist Is a Hit Restaurateur

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2176 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Borgo sits on one of those blocks in the high 20s that you swear you’ve never been down before.
  • On one occasion, my server was a painter who used to bartend at The Odeon, as painters have done for decades.
  • Sources indicate that the twist is that my server’s art was also hanging on the walls of Borgo, as was his daughter’s art.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Borgo sits on one of those blocks in the high 20s that you swear you’ve never been down before. The restaurant opened in 2024 but feels like it’s been there forever, a place with a natural hum and not an ounce of perspiration. Its clientele is specific but unpredictable; when I went there this summer for lunch with a movie producer, we spotted a powerful name-brand media executive, an architectural bigwig who designs the homes of billionaires, and a two-time Academy Award–winning actor. A few nights later, I sat near Walter Isaacson, who’s a regular. And don’t just take it from Elon Musk’s biographer. Matthew Schneier, the chief restaurant critic at Newly introduced York magazine, recently named Borgo the city’s best all-around restaurant.

On one occasion, my server was a painter who used to bartend at The Odeon, as painters have done for decades. He met Ross Bleckner there, and David Salle. He used to have a massive loft studio in Williamsburg, but as rents went up, he moved deeper into Brooklyn, to Fort Greene, where he built a studio in his basement.

Sources indicate that the twist is that my server’s art was also hanging on the walls of Borgo, as was his daughter’s art. That’s because he was Andrew Tarlow—the painter and restaurateur who kick-started the Brooklyn aesthetic with his restaurant Diner and, yes, also owns Borgo.

After launching that instant hit in an old, reclaimed diner, Tarlow opened five more era-defining Brooklyn spots before finally venturing into Manhattan with Borgo. All along, he’s still been the artist who got a job at The Odeon so that he could meet his heroes. He’s still painting away in his brownstone, doodling on notepads during concept meetings. He’s had highlights recently at galleries such as Tiwa Select; he’s loosely associated with the Galerie Sardine extended universe; and he’s someone whose work I’ve been told about for years by those in the know.

As they put it, Tarlow is an emerging artist who happens to own the best all-around restaurant in Manhattan, as well as a bunch of other successful spots in Brooklyn.

“I realized, opening Borgo, that I really loved working in restaurants—and not that I had forgotten, but I hadn’t actually worked services in a while until I opened,” Tarlow told me during a studio visit. “And then, in a similar way, I think—I love making paintings. I actually will paint forever, no matter what happens.”.

Recent findings suggest that the studio had dozens of unstretched canvases heaped on the ground, some still rolled up, and others hanging via a pin on the studio wall. They revealed figures grappling with pain in fierce color-blocked fields, automatic-painting abstractions, faces fading into other faces. One painting was a portrait of the artist Joe Bradley, a friend.

The studio is in the basement of the Fort Greene brownstone where Tarlow has lived for two decades with his wife, Kate Huling, raising four kids in a kind of neo-boho paradise. There were no studio assistants, no art handlers, no frames, no boxes, no packaging—just the artist and the work.

“It was kind of just as chaotic as everything else there, but in the most perfect warm embrace of a way. I saw the pure energy that he put into his paintings and the stories that they told,” claims Alex Tieghi-Walker, the founder of Tiwa Select, calling from London. “So many artists could be quite—rightfully so, but quite precious with their works. And I love that Andrew was just like, ‘Oh, pull out the ones you’re taking and just take them in an Uber home.’”.

Tarlow grabbed at a canvas bare-handed, one with a bit of a conceptual bent, and put it up on an easel.

“I’ve had this up on the wall for a while now, and I just continued to look at it because I’m happy with it. I’m also a little unsettled—I mean, I’m showing you the inside of my drawers. I’m also a little unsettled by how far it’s gone abstract-wise.”.

He told me he couldn’t really do his other job, the restaurant job, without painting at odd hours. They’re totally separate, but complementary in a cosmic way.

“What are the processes? Like you stated, for some people, it’s nine to five. Then you listen to the news, smoke a cigarette, drink coffee. It’s either working or it’s not. The door either opens or it’s not,” Tarlow said, gesturing around to his studio. “But I’m going to go here every day, and I’m going to push some paint on canvas.”.

It has been revealed that diner opened in 1999, a few years after Tarlow moved to the desolate southern tip of Broadway in Williamsburg—where the crumbling street dead-ends into the East River. While looking for a cheap studio space, he found a 6,000-square-foot loft across the street from an abandoned diner from the 1920s. The loft’s landlord bought the diner, and in 1999, Tarlow opened Diner with then partner Mark Firth—and watched as it was patronized by only the artists across the street.

“You could stand outside the restaurant in those days and not see a single person walk by,” he told Bon Appetit in 2010.

Sources indicate that tarlow kept expanding. He opened Marlow & Sons, and then the butcher shop and specialty food store Marlow & Daughters. He founded a bakery, She Wolf, and a literary magazine, Diner Journal. He operated the restaurant at the Wythe Hotel, but only for a few years. Instead of doing the easy thing, Vegas-ifying Diner in some upcoming development on the Williamsburg waterfront, he got even weirder, opening a nautical bar called Achilles Heel in a far-out corner of Greenpoint.

Sources indicate that A dealer with a gallery in Tribeca was the first, but far from the last, to tell me I had to check out Tarlow’s paintings. After an introduction was brokered, Tarlow invited me to lunch at Borgo this past summer. The restaurant has many fantastic pork-laden dishes, but we ate almost entirely vegetables, as well as one very elegant, simple piece of fish. A summer lunch. We fell into an easy patter, talking about exhibitions, other artists—but mostly his painting practice. He’d been working on Long Island, not on the East End but in the middle. He’d had a few shows. There was discussion of representation. He spoke about all this with an unpracticed earnestness and complete confidence. He sounded like a very prominent emerging artist, which, at 56, he is.

“I don’t know if it’s just age or time, or I was too much of a young person, or a young mind, but I’ve been more secure with my ability to hold all these things in the same time,” he told me back in the studio. “I can go work tonight in the restaurant and feel perfectly confident in that work, and I can show you this work and feel perfectly confident in this work. Whereas, I think, as a young person, I felt like, Am I fake?”.

Sometimes it’s not the enfant terrible who breaks out—it’s the working parent, the person with a desk job, the successful entrepreneur who back-ends into revolutionary art making. Think William Carlos Williams writing “The Red Wheelbarrow” while working as a doctor in Rutherford, Newly introduced Jersey. Or Ruth Asawa making art in her kitchen while raising six children in San Francisco. Or Jeff Koons working on Wall Street in order to earn money to make his sculptures. Having a demanding job actually granted them the freedom to be artists. Tarlow started drawing during restaurant concept meetings.

Sometimes Tarlow hangs his own paintings upstairs in his brownstone’s salon room, or at his house on Long Island, to see what they look like in the wild. The paintings have a confident thrust to them, with the colors bold-blocked in a way that reminds me of Albert Oehlen, drawing from Roman and Greek mythology in Twombly-esque riffs: visages multiplying and fading like a Kippenberger-ian pomo ride into the ether. Sure, any painter who’s spent time in Europe since the 1990s has wanted to be Martin Kippenberger. But Tarlow has an actual connection to him: Like Tarlow, Kippenberger was a lover of Italian food and good wine, and he made art to hang in restaurants. And like Tarlow, Kippenberger was a restaurant owner, balancing his studio practice with running Capri, a Venice, California, spot in which he invested after moving to Los Angeles in 1989. According to those present at the time, Kippenberger became a part-owner of the place because, as the artist put it, “You can’t get a decent Bolognese in Los Angeles.”.

Recent findings suggest that as a bartender at The Odeon, Tarlow maintained a working painting studio but found it hard to produce art. After opening Diner, he skipped painting sessions in favor of opening businesses and starting a family. Once that duality settled, he started drawing on the move, carrying sketchbooks and working through potential paintings. Eventually, once the kids got old enough, he built out a studio in a nook of his 19th-century basement.

Recent findings suggest that “I really started painting back downstairs. Let’s just say, after dinner, it was 8 p.m. and they were watching Nemo. No one actually needs me, they’re totally happy. My wife’s up there, everyone’s laughing, giggling with little fish,” he said. “And I can just walk down here and do my thing. Having it in my house for sure is the only way I could do this amount of work, and for sure even get to this place. Because I do think you have to do a certain amount of work to get to this place unless you’re just a born prodigy. But when you think about the genius of Picasso or whomever, he made a million fucking paintings.”.

Tarlow didn’t really show anyone his work for a long time.

“I met Andrew socially. I knew his restaurants way before I knew Andrew. And one day he was like, ‘Come and see my studio,’” Tieghi-Walker tells me. “It did not surprise me at all that he had an art studio in his basement and that these were the types of works he was creating.”.

Recent findings suggest that the show at Tiwa Select was on view right as Tarlow was getting ready to open Borgo. There was a certain amount of unconscious transference, Tarlow told me. For the Tiwa dinner, instead of creating name placards, the artist hand-sketched an artwork of each guest’s name on the paper tablecloth. Now, when a regular makes a reservation at Borgo, Tarlow will elegantly sketch out their name on the paper tablecloth.

In a recent development, the showcasing of his art at Borgo marks the first time Tarlow has put his own work on the premises of his own restaurant. Tarlow doesn’t exactly promote this. When I asked about it, he told me that only one of his own works was up at the moment, then changed the subject. Alex Levy, the media strategist and theater producer, has been a regular at Borgo since it opened. “Borgo is the grown-up Platonic ideal of what a restaurant can be,” he said. After several visits, Levy, who also collects a bit of contemporary art, noticed what was on the walls.

“I complimented one of the paintings, and Andrew remarked, ‘It’s by my daughter.’ And then he pointed to another one and said, ‘That’s by me,’” Levy notes. “I had no idea that there’s this whole other part of him.”.

Sources indicate that like Tarlow, Levy balances two seemingly divergent but strangely complementary careers—as a speechwriter on one hand, a Tony Award winner on the other—and Tarlow invited him to see his studio on Long Island. Levy bought a painting immediately. Seeing the studio, Levy notes, helped him realize, to some extent, what the special sauce is behind a place like Borgo. It’s for incredibly confident, hyperproductive creative types, run by an artist who has complete faith in his ability to work.

And for Tarlow, the focus and passion in one arena lead right into the passion for the other.

In a recent development, “I’m also being very present for your needs in the same way as I’m trying to be very present with these paintings,” he noted. “They’re not separate boats. When the restaurant’s working, I feel creative inside of it.”.

It has been revealed that super Mario Galaxy (both the original and the sequel) are beloved by fans. These titles originally launched on the Wii, and Nintendo rereleased both for the Switch. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The next era of the "James Bond" film franchise is finally taking shape. After years of wondering who will be suiting up as our newly introduced 007, Robert Pattinson has officially been cast as the next James Bond, taking over for Daniel Craig following his final entry with "No Time to Die," which came out way back in 2021. A lot has happened since then, including Amazon buying the rights to the property. Now, with a new lead actor in place, it's time to get the rest of the pieces of the puzzle locked in. That includes finding Bond's boss.

It has been revealed that historically, this has been the one they call M. Originally portrayed by Bernard Lee in the earliest Bond films, the codename given to the person behind the major desk at MI6 is an important one, as they head up the 00 program. Thus, M is the one who gives Bond his assignments and, at times, even helps him out in the field. It's an important role, one that has been played by the likes of Dame Judi Dench and Oscar-nominee Ralph Fiennes.

There's much to be done. Director Denis Villeneuve also has to find an actor to play the villain in Pattinson's "James Bond" movie, but M is a longer commitment, a multi-picture deal. It's a significant responsibility. So, who should play the role alongside Pattinson? Who should be the one to help guide 007 through his next several missions for her majesty's secret service?

In a recent development, we're going to go over a handful of options, ranging from very obvious to unlikely yet intriguing. Let's get into it.

Sources indicate that "The amount of time I have wanted to be M. I'm not sure who I need to call...".

In a recent development, those are the words of Olivia Colman speaking to British Vogue in 2023. She wants the role. She's very well qualified for the role. If everyone wants to make this easy, why not just offer her the role? Sometimes, the easiest answer is also a very good answer. That not every actor who campaigns openly for a role should get it, but we're not just talking about any old actor here.

According to recent reports, colman is responsible for one of the most shocking Oscars upsets of all time when she took home Best Actress for "The Favourite." But it was more shocking because the Academy recognized Colman's impressive work over the rest of the pack. Ever since, she's been on a tear, turning in outstanding performances in everything from "The Lost Daughter" to "Paddington in Peru." Heck, she even ate up some screen time in Marvel's otherwise very disappointing series "Secret Invasion.".

But Colman has been doing it at a very high level for years, long before she won an Oscar. "Hot Fuzz," "The Iron Lady," "Broadchurch." You name it, Colman is one of the best parts of everything she's in. Beyond that, she could bring both a seriousness to the role of M, which is required, while at the same time allowing for a playful dynamic with Bond. Colman feels like a slam dunk. It just so happens that the person campaigning for the role is very much right for the role. That's not always the case.

Industry observers note that if Denis Villeneuve or Amazon want to go with a distinguished, male British actor who could be older and wiser than Robert Pattinson's Bond, one capable of being both convincingly stern and charming, Colin Firth is the man. An Oscar-winning actor who is almost too easy to picture sitting at a major desk behind a padded burgundy door, this is another "the obvious choice can also be the right choice" pick.

It has been revealed that we have an actor here capable of delivering exposition, as M often has to, in a way that would be entertaining, as Firth could read the phone book and it would be engaging. But let's not forget that Firth politely destroyed fools in "Kingsman: The Secret Service," too, and that movie owes a lot to the "James Bond" franchise. What's more, it proved that Firth looks absolutely fantastic in an expensive suit, an key quality of a good M.

His resume speaks for itself. "A Single Man," "The King's Speech," and even "Mamma Mia!" prove that Firth is one of the finest actors of the last 30 years. There's zero question as to whether or not he's qualified to be M. So, it begs the question: Is he right for M? If we're looking to address that question in the traditional sense, then the answer is a resounding yes. The shoe fits and it fits well. Simple as that.

Recent findings suggest that if it weren't for Judi Dench playing M so damn well for so damn long, we might have to have the utterly irritating "let's gender-swap M" conversation. Fortunately, that's not the world we live in. Bearing that in mind, it's going to be damn hard for anyone to argue against Tilda Swinton bossing around Robert Pattinson while dressed to the nines. What's not to like about that?

Recent findings suggest that swinton won a Best Supporting Actress Oscar for "Michael Clayton" so, much like many of the other performers on that list, she's Oscar-caliber. That almost feels like a must for M. Setting that aside, Swinton brings a domineering, powerful quality to so many of her best roles. Even so, she's a bit of a chameleon, which is partially what would make her an interesting M. It's not hard to imagine her playing an MI6 agent who used to work in the field before taking a desk job, yet she still has that darkness behind her eyes from yesteryear.

Oddly, it's Swinton's transformation into the Ancient One" in "Doctor Strange" that might make the best case here. She can do powerful yet quiet without having to be at the center of the action, and she can absolutely handle being a part of a giant, globally popular franchise. Really, there's nothing this role requires that she couldn't do, seemingly with ease.

It has been revealed that some might argue Swinton would be better as a "Bond" villain. That certainly wouldn't upset me, but it might be subverting expectations a bit to have her as Bond's buttoned-up boss. She could also help bring something fresh to the role for this fresh era.

It has been revealed that and now we arrive at the most obvious answer. Does that make it the wrong answer? Using history as our guide, absolutely not. Ralph Fiennes made his entry into the "James Bond" franchise in 2012's "Skyfall" before fully taking over as M in "Spectre" following the death of Judi Dench's M. (May she rest in peace.) So, why replace a perfectly great actor in the role if we don't have to?

It has been revealed that let's not forget that the "James Bond" franchise is notorious for bringing actors back in roles even after reboots. Dench as M for both Pierce Brosnan and Daniel Craig's Bonds. Desmond Llewelyn was Q for every Bond except Craig. That's the nature of the beast as it exists. If Amazon doesn't totally buck tradition, it could easily bring back Fiennes for another go-around. And why not? He's already proven he can do it, he's a stellar actor, and he's arguably as popular as ever.

He's also an actor who seems to really understand the role. "Spectre" was going to make M the villain until Finnes refused. That, to this longtime fan, demonstrates a real understanding of who M is. On top of that, Fiennes is very familiar with shouldering the weight of a major movie franchise, having previously played Voldemort in the "Harry Potter" movies. The only reason to not do this is if Amazon and Denis Villeneuve truly and completely want to hit the major red reset button, which frankly seems likely.

It has been revealed that but if not? The debate could be settled before it even gets started.

Last, but certainly not least, we arrive at the choice that's both decidedly out-of-the-box yet technically in the very box we're talking about. Pierce Brosnan previously played James Bond in four movies stretching from 1995 to 2002. His "GoldenEye" remains the most important box office hit in "James Bond" history, in addition to being a beloved entry in the franchise. But Brosnan's run was uneven and ended on a sour note with "Die Another Day." Perhaps playing M would give him a shot at redemption?

Industry observers note that let's get some things out of the way up top. Yes, it might be a little weird to have a former 007 play M, but it's not that much stranger than fully ignoring continuity in order to have the same actor play M for multiple Bonds. More importantly, Brosnan absolutely looks the part. The man, well into his 70s, still looks better in a suit than most of us could ever hope to. He's got an authoritative on-screen presence, but he's also got that charm that could work wonders for M.

Recent findings suggest that brosnan feels he was never good enough as James Bond. I would humbly argue that the scripts weren't always good enough for his James Bond, not the other way around. Why not use the past to help build a future for the franchise? Let Brosnan bring his experience to the role and mentor Robert Pattinson's 007. The meta nature of it all might add something to their dynamic.

The question of whether or not Brosnan would want to take on the role is another one entirely, but it's a wild card idea that's just inspired enough to be a whole lot of fun.

The new "James Bond" movie doesn't have a release date, but stay tuned.
