10 Bad Movies With Great Trailers

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1527 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Screenrant

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that every movie, even those as massive as the upcoming Avengers: Doosmday or Dune: Part Three, needs an exciting trailer.
  • Take the teaser for Star Wars: Episode VII - The Force Awakens, for example.
  • Recent findings suggest that that trailer was praised for its editing, teasing the story of The Force Awakens (and the newly introduced characters) just the right amount.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that every movie, even those as massive as the upcoming Avengers: Doosmday or Dune: Part Three, needs an exciting trailer. After all, it’s these brief looks at the film that are crucial in convincing audiences that a given title is worth their time (and money, given how expensive movie theaters are these days). Not only that, but trailers can be their very own events, too.

Take the teaser for Star Wars: Episode VII - The Force Awakens, for example. The 90-second first look was released by Apple on iTunes, who had paid significant money to be the ones to release the trailer first. And, predictably, the trailer’s debut crashed the manufacturer’s servers, making some fans wait to watch it till after they were fixed.

Recent findings suggest that that trailer was praised for its editing, teasing the story of The Force Awakens (and the newly introduced characters) just the right amount. The quality of the trailer seemed to transfer to the movie itself, too, as Episode VII received 93% and 84% with critics and audiences respectively on Rotten Tomatoes.

However, not every good trailer translates to the film. Some movies have had amazing trailers, but the actual movie itself failed to live up to the hype. Both the Marvel Cinematic Universe and Zack Snyder’s DCEU have been guilty of this at times, releasing trailers that were far superior to the movie at hand.

The hype for David Ayer’s Suicide Squad was massive prior to the film’s release. That’s even as Suicide Squad’s in-universe predecessor, Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice, generally failed to excite audiences (although a small portion was extremely happy with the direction Snyder took those characters).

Sources indicate that typically, one would expect the next movie in the franchise to suffer a dip as a result of Batman v Superman’s mistakes (receiving a 28% on Rotten Tomatoes). Instead, the opposite happened, with Suicide Squad earning $749 million from a $175 million budget, thus making Ayer’s film more profitable than Batman v Superman (the latter made more money but had a significantly higher budget).

Arguably the main reason for Suicide Squad defying the norm in this regard is its trailers. The trailers were exceptionally edited, equipped with well-known songs that fit the dark and moody tone of the universe and the antiheroes that make up the Suicide Squad. Ultimately, they promised a movie that simply didn’t exist, as the final product was poorly edited and tonally misguided (essentially the exact opposite of the trailer).

Recent findings suggest that the release of a Max Payne movie in 2008 was an attempt by 20th Century Fox to capitalize on the popularity of the video game series with the same name. For a moment, it seemed that the studio were on track to become very successful with that mission. The trailer for Max Payne captured the feel of the video game perfectly, all while making the movie look suspenseful and compelling.

The final product, however, was the exact opposite of that. Max Payne deviated greatly from the video game, which isn’t necessarily a problem, but the decisions that the filmmakers made largely didn’t pay off. Not only that, but the trailer made the action look unique and entertaining, but in the film, these sequences are often where Max Payne struggles the most, with an over reliance on CGI (which wasn’t very well done anyway).

Recent findings suggest that it’s easy to forget that, outside of the Deadpool films, Ryan Reynolds’ career has been thoroughly hit or miss (more so the latter, quite frankly). Yet, in 2013, it looked as if Reynolds might just buck that trend with RIPD. The trailer made the film look like a spiritual sequel to Men in Black, equipped with two compelling leads in Reynolds and Jeff Bridges. The film itself, however, is one of the worst of the 2010s.

In a recent development, M. Night Shyamalan diverted from his typical genre of films with the release of The Last Airbender in 2010. Despite high anticipation, this film failed to excite audiences (something that was predictable to long-term fans, many of whom were skeptical of turning the series into a feature-length film). The Last Airbender fit an entire twenty-episode season into one movie, which makes the story feel rushed and incomplete as a result.

Industry observers note that however, the trailer did well to hide these issues. The visuals looked interesting, and the trailer did enough to convince audiences that Shyamalan’s next adventure may be worth watching. It’s a shame, then, that the film failed to live up to its promise, delivering a flat and convoluted adaptation of an animated series that deserved much better.

Industry observers note that the Terminator franchise was massively popular in the 80s and 90s with the release of both The Terminator and T2: Judgment Day. Although the third film in the trilogy wasn’t as well received, the franchise was still held in high regard. It’s no wonder, then, that Warner Bros. were keen on bringing the world of the Terminators back, this time with a prequel film.

Terminator Salvation tells the story of the war between humans and the AI that is hinted at (and briefly shown) in the original Terminator trilogy. The idea of the film was brilliant, especially as it finally gave adult John Connor a chance to be the leading man. The trailer showed just that, thus highlighting how much potential the movie had. It’s a shame, then, that Salvation’s trailer ended up being so misleading, promising a film that was much more compelling than the final product.

Recent findings suggest that another film by M. Night Shyamalan (and arguably one of the weakest entries in his filmography), Old tells the story of a group of strangers who begin rapidly aging while on a beach. The trailer felt like classic Shyamalan, with plenty of mystery, intrigue, and an exciting premise to boot. However, Old ended up being a complete misfire in every way, especially with its twist, which was disappointing and confusing.

The 2000s were the decade of superhero reboots for Warner Bros. and DC. First, Christopher Nolan revamped DC’s most popular hero with Batman Begins, which brought the Caped Crusader into the 21st century with a film that finally took itself seriously. Batman Begins was hugely successful, so it’s no wonder that the studio looked to release a Superman movie as rapidly as possible afterward.

According to recent reports, superman Returns brought Christopher Reeve’s iteration of the iconic hero back, but this time with a fresh set of actors (all of whom are impressive in the film, even amidst the broader issues with the story). At the same time, viewers didn’t have to see Reeve’s movies in order to understand the plot of Superman Returns or become invested in the characters. However, the film itself squandered all potential, with a story that was too slow-paced. Not only that, but Bryan Singer’s movie also lacked originality, and ended up sticking too closely to the Superman films of the 70s and 80s.

Recent findings suggest that the trailer for the movie promised something completely different, however. In fact, Superman Returns’ trailer was an idealized version of the film, showing what it could have been, but ultimately was not. The trailer was epic, balancing nostalgia with freshness, something that the actual movie gets badly wrong.

The more recent Alien movies have been relatively divisive. Some audiences clearly appreciated the unique direction the franchise was heading in, while others were critical of the overall vision of Ridley Scott. Alien: Covenant’s trailer revealed great promise, and even made a few fans who weren’t impressed with the previous installments think that this one might be different. However, Covenant only regressed from its predecessor, proving to be an overly complicated film that failed to capture what makes the Alien franchise so good in the first place.

Recent findings suggest that the Marvel Cinematic Universe has had an up-and-down time since the release of Avengers: Endgame in 2019. Thor: Love and Thunder firmly falls into the latter category, going way over the top with its humor and, even worse, had clearly unfinished special effects. If Thor: Ragnarok revealed the very best of Taika Waititi, then Love and Thunder highlights the complete opposite, showcasing all the director’s worst tendencies.

Recent findings suggest that the trailer gave little indication that Love and Thunder would turn out so poorly, however. In fact, the trailer made the film look epic and exciting, and teased Jane Foster’s comeback spectacularly. Once again, though, Foster’s role in the film was underwhelming, and it felt like a wasted opportunity overall.

According to recent reports, 2011s Battle Los Angeles was made in the same vein as the Transformers films of the same era. Battle Los Angeles featured a city being destroyed, people fleeing in panic, and huge-scale action amidst the rubble. The trailer made Battle Los Angeles look epic and akin to the very best of what the Transformers franchise had to offer. However, the movie itself failed spectacularly, with poor shaky cam action and a script that was as generic as they come.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, if your lawn is buried under a blanket of fallen leaves like mine, raking them up has likely turned a routine chore into a real slog.
  • Industry observers note that and while my go-to steel rake has been my lifesaver, I often worry I might be causing damage to my healthy lawn in the process.
  • Industry observers note that I called on an expert to shed light on this and offer top tips on how to rake wet leaves without pulling up blades of grass.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, if your lawn is buried under a blanket of fallen leaves like mine, raking them up has likely turned a routine chore into a real slog. When wet conditions set in, clearing leaves off the grass often turns into a time-consuming hassle.

Industry observers note that and while my go-to steel rake has been my lifesaver, I often worry I might be causing damage to my healthy lawn in the process. This is especially the case when the leaves all clump together, making it a challenge to leave my grass spotless and debris-free.

Industry observers note that I called on an expert to shed light on this and offer top tips on how to rake wet leaves without pulling up blades of grass. So before you get out to tackle your leaves on your lawn, here are expert-approved tips this season.

Industry observers note that with wet weather making lawn care challenging, is raking damp leaves actually safe for my grass? “Yes, although wet leaves are heavier, stick together, and can be much more difficult to rake, blow, or vacuum,” states Karen Musgrave, Horticulturalist at Hicks Nurseries.

According to recent reports, “The bigger concern for your lawn is allowing a thick layer of leaves to remain there for an extended period of time. A heavy mat of wet leaves can block sunlight and air from reaching the grass and trap excess moisture underneath.”.

A heavy mat of wet leaves can block sunlight and air from reaching the grass and trap excess moisture underneath.

Sources indicate that in addition, leaving wet leaves sitting on your lawn over time can smother the grass, blocking essential nutrients from reaching the roots and making it prone to mold and fungal diseases. This can lead to patchy or thinning grass that will need urgent repair come springtime.

So what is the correct way to rake wet leaves without pulling up grass and harming my lawn? Experts agree that choosing the right tools is essential to do the job — and keep your yard intact.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

“If the lawn is wet, avoid being overly aggressive with a rake because you can pull at the grass,” advises Musgrave. “ For the lawn, I would choose a lightweight leaf rake with a wide head rather than a heavier garden rake.

Recent findings suggest that “It gives you more control around garden beds, shrubs, and other areas where you don’t necessarily want to blow everything around. A smaller or narrower rake is especially helpful for removing leaves that have collected between plants in the landscape without damaging them.”.

It’s also notable to invest in a good-quality rake; aluminum or plastic rakes are best for most leaf cleanups. Unlike leaf blowers, a durable rake is affordable, easy, and practical to use, and doesn’t need fuel or batteries.

Sources indicate that if in doubt, though, check out these different types of rakes suitable for your yard. For more top tips, check out how to rake leaves the easy way — 7 tips and tricks.

A top tip is to (ideally) rake on a dry day, as the leaves will be easier to gather and less of a chore.

Also, you don’t have to clear every single leaf off your lawn, since keeping a few around can actually benefit your garden plants. “Don’t blow or rake every leaf out of your garden beds just for the sake of making them spotless,” adds Musgrave.

“Some leaf litter can be beneficial for the soil as it breaks down and adds organic matter. It can also provide overwintering habitat for beneficial insects. You don’t want leaves piled so heavily that they smother smaller plants, but a light layer can be left in place.”.

Industry observers note that shredding leaves with a lawn mower is another handy trick. Breaking them down into smaller pieces makes it easy to add them to your compost heap and return those valuable nutrients to your yard.

In a recent development, “Excess leaves can also be added to a compost pile rather than bagged and thrown away. Chopping or shredding them first can help them break down more swiftly. The key is to make sure the leaves aren’t so thick they cover the grass and block sunlight and air.”.

Finally, pay attention to bare spots and thin areas. Depending on your grass type and climate, consider overseeding before the harsh winter arrives. “Apply a grass seed that is appropriate for your lawn, lightly rake it into the soil, and keep the area consistently moist while the new grass gets established.

"The cooler temperatures of fall are ideal for establishing grass. Taking care of thin and bare spots now gives new grass time to develop roots before winter and helps create a fuller, healthier lawn for spring.”.

Here’s when to plant grass seed in November to get the best results.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, it’s been quite a year for Curry Barker. In September 2025, he brought his $700,000 horror film to the Toronto International Film Festival, where it sparked a bidding war that Focus Features won for $17 million. That hefty price tag turned into the deal of the century, as “Obsession” went on to become a half-billion-dollar box-office sensation, with audiences growing week to week. It was clear the then 26-year-old “YouTuber” (a moniker Barker rightfully dismisses) was something special. This was not just a flash in the pan, but a real talent with a seemingly boundless number of ideas and movies he wanted to make. His next film, “Anything but Ghosts,” was already in the can by the “Obsession” premiere, a yet-to-be-confirmed third film is in the works, while potential franchises (“Texas Chainsaw Massacre” and “Obsession,” Barker sees the One Wish Willow story device having “Knives Out” anthology-like potential) linger in the background. Related Stories Director Brian Duffield Had to Find a Upcoming Form of Visual Storytelling for ‘Whalefall’ How ‘Paper Tiger’ Evolved When Jeremy Strong and Anne Hathaway Couldn’t Reprise Their ‘Armageddon Time’ Roles.

Which is why it’s interesting that Hollywood’s hottest new director took time out from editing (he’s cutting “Ghosts” himself) and writing (“I have my next thing that I’m working on — I’m really excited about it, and nobody knows anything about it, which is super exciting”), and an unexpected Oscar campaign (“Obsession” is a legit contender for Best Picture, Actress, and Original Screenplay nominations), to make a 5-minute short film, “Mama Bear.” On this week’s episode of the Filmmaker Toolkit Podcast, Barker talked about how the success of “Obsession” interrupted his established flow of churning out short-form content for his popular YouTube channel.

According to recent reports, “I have two or three short films where I’m like, ‘Oh man, this all took off really quickly, and I have this short film idea I’ve been dying to do,” said Barker on Toolkit. “I actually have no time to do those short films, and then justifying if it be would be worth my time to do them when I need to be writing this, I need to be editing this, and I need to be doing press for this.”.

It’s less about Barker’s desire to scratch the itch of the shorts he never got to make, but more about a hesitancy to step away completely from the iterative process by which he learned his craft — justifying the brief time he took off to make “Mama Bear” because he felt the need to sketch.

“It’s fun to have that playground because the features are bigger stakes,” remarked Barker. “We were like, ‘Okay, this is a short film: We can do weird stuff. Let’s come up with crazy rules that don’t make sense, and experiment.’”.

In a recent development, barker and his “Mama Bear” cinematographer — his young brother Riley, who worked on the “Obsession” camera department — created different rules for the camera, as Curry is still trying to hone his discipline for storytelling within longer takes. Not only would they shoot a narrow 4:3 aspect ratio, but the Barker brothers denied themselves the ability to move the camera left, right, up, down, or dolly in.

“I do have a lot to learn,” mentioned Barker of making “Mama Bear.” “It’s so funny because I was having dinner and I told someone, ‘Oh, I’d love to shadow on Ari Aster’s set.’ And someone was like, ‘Well, you’re Curry Barker, what are you going to shadow for?’”.

His 2026 meteoric rise has allowed Barker to collect a group of more experienced peers he views as mentors — including Aster, Bill Hader, Zach Cregger, and Rian Johnson — and successful producers, like Jason Blum, investing in his career, but he believes there’s a misconception of what comes along with “making it.”.

Industry observers note that “People think that once you’re in this club, you’re in the club, and everyone talks to everyone. But no — you’re in a bubble, and I want to know how Zach Cregger writes his outline. I want to watch him do it,” said Barker. “You’re all alone. Your process is your own, and you figure this stuff out on your own. Once you get into this league, there’s no one telling you, ‘Well, actually you do it like this, this, and this.’ It’s whatever you learned all along your journey; that’s your process.”.

Industry observers note that one of the most impressive things about the self-taught Barker’s journey is how swiftly he turned himself into a successful actor/writer/director/editor. In 2018, when Barker left Alabama to come to Los Angeles to pursue a career in movies, he saw himself as an actor. Despite all the story scenarios dancing around his head, the idea that he would become a screenwriter was laughable.

Sources indicate that “I never would’ve thought I was a screenwriter. I didn’t make great grades. I made Cs and Ds, and I wasn’t the best in English class,” said Barker, who naively assumed professional writers were the kids who won spelling bees: “I just thought to be respected as a writer you have to be that.” Barker credits taking screenwriter Aaron Sorkin’s MasterClass as what opened his eyes. “It was the first time I thought, ‘I can do this, too.’ It’s really just about being creative and cracking a story, and there are rules, there’s structure.”.

Sources indicate that directing organically grew out of Barker pulling together collaborators to shoot sketches and shorts for him to act in. Barker, half-joking, likes to say he realized one day that what he was doing was directing, and that he both enjoyed “telling people what to do” and had a knack for it.

Recent findings suggest that what Barker accomplishes in a single shot — establishing a tonal balance that teeters between horror and comedy, combining blocking and camera movement to edit within the frame — is remarkably sophisticated. But Barker, who studies and strives for what masters like Kiyoshi Kurosawa can accomplish, promptly claims he fell short in “Obsession.”.

Sources indicate that “Things that you might think we pulled off [with longer takes in ‘Obsession’], we reshot,” mentioned Barker, who on the podcast described in detail a key early scene between Bear (Michael Johnston) and Nikki (Inde Navarrette) in the bedroom that had to be reshot because the action took too long to unfold. “I think Ari [Aster] said once that if you realize you needed to give this information in four seconds, but then it took 25 seconds, you’re stuck with 25 seconds.”.

Curry Barker, the editor, is Curry Barker, the director’s harshest critic, giving him a bird’s-eye view of what he believes is the director’s inability to envision the required pacing of how a scene will play on screen, even if it might feel unnaturally fast on set.

“Every single oner that I’ve shot in my career has been a problem in the edit,” said Barker. “I think there’s two ways to fail at something. You can either fail, realize that it didn’t work, get scared of it, and then be like, ‘Well, in my last film I did a bunch of oners and then it killed me in the edit, so I’m not going to do that anymore.’ Or you can fail, realize how you did it wrong, and try to get better at that for the next time.”.

As Barker discussed at the Future of Filmmaking Summit last month, that iterative process is key to how he got where he is, and it’s a mindset he clearly hasn’t given up. When asked how “Obsession” would have been different if he had more money, Barker doesn’t talk about locations, sets, special or visual effects, or scenes he envisioned that he couldn’t pull off — in terms of scale, he likes both writing and directing within set limitations.

“I would’ve reshot everything,” Barker answered without hesitation. “If I was finishing the edit before we got into TIFF, and you were like, ‘Dude, this is really good, we really love this movie, we think it has potential, but we want to give you $10 million to reshoot the whole thing, I would be like, ‘Deal.’ I would take it.”.

“I think it’s so funny to look back and think about that now,” Barker catches himself, knowing he’s talking about a film that broke the box office and catapulted his career. “Now I wouldn’t change anything because I would be too scared to touch it.”.

6 Best Books From the Year 2020 That Are 10/10 Masterpieces

  • Nobody needs to be reminded of what 2020 felt like.
  • That became my routine for the rest of the year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that feel free to connect with him or check out his work. He's everywhere — Upwork, YouTube, Spotify, SoundCloud, Collider, LinkedIn, Instagram.

Nobody needs to be reminded of what 2020 felt like. The days blurred together, the news got worse every morning, and most of us ran out of indicates to binge by April. I remember sitting on my bedroom floor one night, scrolling through my phone for the hundredth time, and feeling completely empty. So I put it face down, picked up a book I’d been ignoring for months, and read until two in the morning.

That became my routine for the rest of the year. Books turned into a kind of escape hatch, a way to live somewhere else for a few hours when going anywhere wasn’t allowed. Looking back, it’s funny how many good ones came out in such a bad year. These six are the ones that kept me firm the most, and I’m still a little grateful to each of them.

A group of old college friends rents a huge mansion by the sea for the summer, bringing their kids along. The parents spend most of their time drunk, lazy, and embarrassing their children. The kids, led by a sharp teenager named Evie, are so disgusted that they make a game of hiding which adult belongs to which child. Then a monstrous storm rolls in, and while the grown-ups fall apart, the children decide to save themselves.

It has been revealed that lydia Millet wrote A Children’s Bible as a story about climate change, but it never feels like a lecture. Evie’s little brother, Jack, carries around an illustrated Bible and starts seeing its stories come true around him, which adds a strange, almost magical layer. The book is short, and it moves fast. It was also a finalist for the 2020 National Book Award, and it reads like a warning from the next generation to ours.

Recent findings suggest that sportcoat is an old church deacon in a Brooklyn housing project in 1969, and he is almost never sober. One afternoon, in front of everyone, he walks up to Deems Clemens, a young drug dealer he once coached in baseball, and shoots him in the ear. Nobody knows why, including Sportcoat himself, who can’t remember a thing. Suddenly, the whole neighborhood gets pulled into the mess, from the police to the local mob.

If that setup sounds grim, Deacon King Kong will surprise you, because it’s one of the funniest books on this list. James McBride fills the projects with gossiping church ladies, crooked cops, and a man who argues daily with the ghost of his dead wife. Aside from all the jokes, though, there’s real love for a community that people often wrote off. Oprah Winfrey picked it for her book club, and it absolutely deserved the spotlight.

The narrator of Homeland Elegies shares a name with his author, Ayad Akhtar. Like Akhtar, he’s a writer born in America to Pakistani parents, and he grows up trying to figure out where he truly belongs. His father is a doctor who once treated Donald Trump in the ’90s and still admires him. Meanwhile, after 9/11, the country they both love starts looking at families like theirs with suspicion.

Because the line between fact and fiction keeps blurring, you’ll often stop and wonder, “Wait, did this really happen?” That’s part of the fun. Akhtar, who already won a Pulitzer Prize for his play Disgraced, writes about money, religion, and identity without ever trying to sound polite. Some chapters feel like long, honest conversations over chai. If you’ve ever felt like a stranger in a place you call home, this one will speak to you directly.

Most people know that William Shakespeare wrote Hamlet. Fewer know that he had a son named Hamnet, who died at just 11 years old in 1596. Hamnet imagines the life of that family before and after the loss. Strangely, Shakespeare’s name never even appears in the book. Instead, the heart of the story is his wife, Agnes, a healer who knows herbs, keeps a falcon, and senses things other people can’t.

Industry observers note that honestly, I’ve never read a book about grief that felt this close to the bone. Maggie O’Farrell spends one entire chapter tracing how the plague traveled from Italy to a small English town, flea by flea, and it’s somehow both beautiful and terrifying. The novel won the 2020 Women’s Prize for Fiction. It was later turned into a film starring Jessie Buckley and Paul Mescal, but read the book first. Trust me on this.

It has been revealed that desiree and Stella Vignes are identical twins from a small Louisiana town where everyone is Black but very light-skinned. At 16, they ran away together to Fresh Orleans. Then their lives split. Desiree eventually returns home with a dark-skinned daughter, while Stella quietly vanishes, starts passing as a white woman, and marries a white man who knows nothing about her past. For years, neither sister knows where the other is.

Industry observers note that what hooked me about The Vanishing Half is how it follows not just the twins but also their daughters, whose paths eventually cross in the most unexpected way. Brit Bennett writes about race, family, and secrets in simple, clear sentences that hit surprisingly hard. Stella’s choice is never painted as fully right or fully wrong.

It has been revealed that growing up in 1980s Glasgow, young Hugh “Shuggie” Bain has two problems. The first is that he’s different from the other boys, softer and gentler, and everyone around him notices. The second, and much bigger one, is his mother, Agnes. She’s glamorous, proud, and fiercely loving, but she’s also slowly drowning in alcohol. The rest of the family gives up on her one by one, but Shuggie keeps trying to save her.

It has been revealed that shuggie Bain won the 2020 Booker Prize, which is even more amazing considering it was Douglas Stuart’s first novel, and dozens of publishers had turned it down. Stuart grew up in Glasgow and lost his own mother to alcoholism, so every page feels painfully real. It’s a heartbreaking book, no doubt about it. But the love between Shuggie and Agnes is so tender that you’ll keep reading, even when it hurts.

Recent findings suggest that four worlds and four completely different ideas of what a good life looks like. This is where you belong, what it would ask of you, and what you would get back in return.

Industry observers note that you belong somewhere old enough that the mountains have names and somebody can still tell you who gave them. Middle-earth is for people who think the right thing is worth doing even when it will not be finished in their lifetime.

Recent findings suggest that you want the sea, a crew, and absolutely nobody telling you where you are allowed to go. The Grand Line is the world for people whose main ambition in life is finding out what is over there.

Recent findings suggest that you would rather be feared and useful than liked and useless. The Continent is a world where the monsters are the straightforward part of the job and the people are where it all gets complicated.

You want the myths to be real and loose in the actual world, and you want to find out at about thirteen that you were never anywhere near as ordinary as everybody kept telling you.

Last month Apple declared major updates coming to Apple Creator Studio in November, and those updates have just arrived, headlined by the addition of MotionVFX in Final Cut Pro and a lot more.

When Apple unveiled its newly introduced MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR last month, it highlighted several big updates coming to Apple Creator Studio’s app suite.

Logic Pro got its update earlier in November, which introduced latest AI features and also the first example of Apple charging for increased AI access via ‘intelligence usage packs.’.

Now today after about a two-week gap, the rest of the Apple Creator Studio updates are rolling out on the App Store.

Pixelmator Pro has added a upcoming Generate Fill feature, which “lets creators transform selected areas of an image using natural language.” And you can edit images from a Final Cut Pro project using Pixelmator’s tools.

Updates for Pages, Keynote, and Numbers are rolling out too with an Intelligent Assistant feature, as well as smaller releases for Apple’s other pro utilities.

To read more on the newly introduced updates, see our previous coverage here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Warning: There are spoilers ahead for Yellowjackets season 4, episode 1, "Hivemind."After one episode of Yellowjackets season 4, the biggest character rule has already been broken by Melissa Kaplan (Hilary Swank). In season 3, Melissa was confirmed as another survivor of the Yellowjackets in the 2020s. After faking her death, she rebooted her life under the name of Kelly, got married to Alex (Jaylee Hamidi), became a mother, and built a new life.

The show's final season opens with Melissa on the run from her old teammates after the violent reunion in season 3 culminated in her killing Van Palmer (Lauren Ambrose). Initially, Melissa and Alex keep a low profile and avoid being found for four weeks, despite a private investigator being hired to track them down.

Melissa then takes a different approach by moving into the house next door to Shauna Sadecki (Melanie Lynskey) in Wiskayok, Latest Jersey. At first, Shauna believes this was a foolish move, only to see that her ex has called the media to their neighborhood, which goes against everything agreed upon in Yellowjackets' 1990s timeline.

A promise that the Yellowjackets made was to not speak to the media about what happened in the wilderness and to stick to a single lie about the story of their survival. This is seen in the season 4 premiere by the survivors having a uniform response to the investigator's questions and not speaking to any of the media bombarding them with questions when they board the plane that will take them back to the United States.

In a recent development, season 1 also set a precedent for this when Shauna and Misty Quigley (Christina Ricci) refuse to speak to Jessica Roberts (Rekha Sharma), who claims to be a reporter, about the true events of what occurred in the wilderness. Jessica is actually a private detective hired by Taissa Turner (Tawny Cypress) to make sure her fellow survivors won't talk while she is running for political office. While she has her fair share of differences with Shauna and Misty, they do stick to their original promise.

This makes it all the more notable that Melissa is now breaking the rule by inviting the media to her home, presumably speaking with them, and one of the Yellowjackets season 4 trailers even shows her and Alex being interviewed on camera. Doing this is yet another way in which Melissa is breaking the trust of the other survivors, which she has already shattered by lying about her death and killing one of them. She is on the cusp of delivering an even worse blow, though.

Recent findings suggest that the other part of the survivors' promise is to keep what happened in the wilderness a secret. By speaking to the media, Melissa has the potential to be the one to finally share the truth with the entire world. Since Yellowjackets season 5 is not happening and this is the conclusion of the series, the truth going public is a viable development for the story's endgame, and it would place the adult characters in a different kind of predicament than they have ever faced before during the final episodes.

Industry observers note that that being said, Melissa is acting out of self-preservation for herself and her family. Introducing herself to the world and telling everyone that she is living next door to Shauna now lets everyone know where they are. It will make it more difficult for the remaining survivors to hurt or kill Melissa and her family in retaliation as a result of this.

How World-Class Filmmaker Andrey Zvyagintsev Came Back to Life for ‘Minotaur’

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • [Editor’s note: This interview was originally published during the 2026 Cannes Film Festival.
  • Sources indicate that world-class Russian filmmaker Andrey Zvyagintsev (“Leviathan”) returned to the Croisette this year in Cannes competition with “Minotaur,” having recovered from a near-fatal illness.
  • According to recent reports, when he left the hospital in Germany in 2022, as he told me while at Cannes this year, he was in a wheelchair.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

[Editor’s note: This interview was originally published during the 2026 Cannes Film Festival. MUBI will release “Minotaur” in theaters on Friday, November 20.].

Sources indicate that world-class Russian filmmaker Andrey Zvyagintsev (“Leviathan”) returned to the Croisette this year in Cannes competition with “Minotaur,” having recovered from a near-fatal illness. After contracting a severe case of COVID in 2021, he reacted badly to the Sputnik vaccine and was put into a medically induced coma for 14 days. When he came out of it, his arms and legs were paralyzed due to Guillain-Barré Syndrome. He lay flat on his back for a year.

According to recent reports, when he left the hospital in Germany in 2022, as he told me while at Cannes this year, he was in a wheelchair. While he states he hasn’t watched TV for 20 years now, “I watched a lot of films online,” he mentioned through an interpreter on the roof of the Palais. “I read some things. I did not know if I would ever be able to walk again, to live again as a normal person. I have still now some consequences. I’m not at my best. I have regained completely the motion of my hands, but I have still a bit of a difficulty walking.” Related Stories If There’s Generative AI in ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth,’ It’s Not the First Time David Fincher’s Used It Trump Renews Backing for Federal Film Tax Credit as Lawmakers Push for Year-End Passage.

But he did manage to shoot his sixth feature film last year, but not in Russia. After nine months of waiting, in the spring of 2023, he let go of one expensive project (“Jupiter”) for which he couldn’t seem to raise funding. “I stated, ‘Let’s put it on ice, we’ll come back to it later. I don’t want to sit and wait for years and years for you to find the money. I want to make a film now.'”.

So instead the filmmaker focused on a parallel project he had also been developing, an adaptation of Claude Chabrol’s 1969 thriller “The Unfaithful Wife,” starring Stéphane Audran as a well-heeled wife cheating on her husband, which was later remade as “Unfaithful” with Richard Gere and Diane Lane. The result, “Minotaur,” is the “Leviathan” Oscar nominee’s first film in nearly a decade, since 2017’s “Loveless.”.

Recent findings suggest that at the same time that the filmmaker was coping with his illness, four years ago, at the start of the Ukraine war, he made the decision to leave Russia and move to Paris. Going home would mean the risk of being considered a traitor or an enemy of the state in Russia. “It might result in us becoming what is called foreign agents; it’s a hard thing,” he said. “Maybe this will happen, maybe not. Let’s not be too pessimistic, but mostly all independent journalists are saying that their oppressions are going to get even harsher, and that I think we have decades ahead of us before things get better.”.

Sources indicate that his 16-year-old had been studying at a French high school in Moscow before the war. “His French was pretty good,” remarked Zvyagintsev. “So it was an obvious choice. And also, my wife [has been] in love with France for a long time, she has been learning French for many years. So it was a choice, also for both of them, and for their future.”.

Sources indicate that how’s his French? “Zero,” he remarked. “The other reason for me was that France is the homeland to cinema; that’s where cinema was born, and also there are so many cinephiles among spectators. Also here in France, directors have the final cut. In the states, it’s much harder to get in a position where you are not censored; it’s not a producer or someone who decides instead of you.”.

The filmmaker set about creating believable Russian locations in Riga, Latvia, which still resembles its neighbor country. “The dormitory suburbs around Riga look exactly like Russian dormitory suburbs,” stated Zvyagintsev. “A Russian eye would not be able to distinguish between Russia and Latvia in this instance. As for interiors, Anton’s flat was constructed as a set, so it’s a constructed set, and the villa where the main characters live is a contemporary building, a very modern one, and you could find something exactly like this anywhere.”.

When it came to finding his cast, the casting director put out a call for Russian characters of a certain age. “Every actor from anywhere who is interested in working with you, they will send you a video presentation,” mentioned Zvyagintsev. “They can be from Argentina, London, Moscow, Paris, wherever. You send them a scene they have to play, and they make a self-tape for you on their iPhone. Before, I despised self-tapes, but it’s convenient, because now with everybody scattered around the world, it’s the only way for us to work. We could not possibly pay for all the people I wanted to check to come to Riga to make a real-life casting. There were people also from Riga who do speak Russian.”.

Industry observers note that one serious issue for Russian actors still living in Russia was the possible repercussions of participating in a Zvyagintsev project. “I would talk to them about the script and show them parts of the script, so that they know what they’re getting involved in, because, of course, they were at risk of getting blacklisted,” he noted. “Most of them, with heartache, refused to take part in the film, but there was one who accepted, and I’m still completely amazed at his courage. It’s the main part, the main character, [actor] Dmitriy Mazurov. I said to him, ‘Are you sure you want to film with me?’ And he said, ‘If I’m not doing this part, I don’t know what I’m doing in acting.'”.

Of course, the filmmaker took a different approach to the Chabrol story. “In the first minute, the story is completely revealed,” he said. “We understand that she is being unfaithful, so then all the film is about observing him, observing her, trying to understand, hesitating, and trying to guess what is going on, and while he observes, the spectator starts doing it along with him. And after the murder, actually, he goes back to this position where he’s mostly observing her reaction to the disappearance of a lover, yeah, and she knows what’s going on, and again it’s about observation.”.

The filmmaker loved one bravura sequence that is 20 minutes long without any dialogue at all. “The sequence after the murder, it’s 20 minutes, even a little bit more, with not one subtitle, so you only observe his actions, and there are no words: it’s extremely cinematic in its essence.”.

Industry observers note that and Zvyagintsev added many telling details from the real world, from corruption to the war. “The Chabrol film is much more classical,” he said. “It follows a pattern: he killed, then he’s discovered, and then he will be punished. And I wanted to break up this classical structure and to invent something different based on our Russian realities.”.

According to recent reports, was shooting the movie a physical challenge? “When you are full of inspiration, when you are searching constantly for solutions, the light, the sets, the performance of the actors, you don’t feel fatigued in the same way,” he said. “There is such a joy in making the film that is, in your head, real. I think it’s the best drug there is.”.

Next up, he will try and resuscitate “Jupiter.” ” I have met some producers who are interested in it,” he mentioned, “so hopefully we will be able to get it moving again.”.

According to recent reports, after 13 long years, GTA 6 is finally here — and it has already become the most acclaimed video game of all time, holding a score of 99 on Metacritic. Since I have a full-time job (and I didn't book time off just to play the game), I've only managed four hours so far... and I'm already in love with the world of Leonida.

If you're playing the game or are planning to, you need the ultimate setup — which includes the best headset and the best controller — to make the most of the experience. I'm playing on my PS5 Slim, and luckily, I get to test these fun peripherals and accessories as part of my job, so who better to advise you on the best tech to use than me?

After 13 years of waiting, Grand Theft Auto VI has arrived. Set in the state of Leonida, with Vice City at its heart, you play Jason and Lucia, two criminals forced into an increasingly dangerous situation as they seek their fortune, discovering the darker side of the sunniest spot in America.

I've spent the last week testing and reviewing the Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited controller and the Sony PlayStation Pulse Wireless Headset, and I highly recommend these for PS5 gamers. But of course, they're brand upcoming and the controller especially isn't the cheapest.

Recent findings suggest that coincidentally, it's also Black Friday week (lucky you!), and I've rounded up some cheaper alternatives so you don't have to spend hours combing through the sales. So, without further ado, here are my headset and controller recommendations for experiencing GTA 6 to its fullest.

Recent findings suggest that I think all PS5 players can agree that the first-party DualSense is, without a doubt, the best controller for the console. That's thanks to its haptic feedback and adaptive triggers that make play feel immersive — but the Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited is the PS5 controller for those who value precision above all else.

One of the biggest advantages is the R5U's customizable layout as it's got four buttons on the back and two on the top, so you can assign frequently used actions to them without moving your thumbs from the sticks. I've found these particularly helpful during cop pursuits and fast-paced missions. Using the rear buttons to, say, accelerate and brake my car feels more natural, too.

The importance of TMR sensors in the R5U's thumbsticks can't be overstated either. They're designed to reduce the traditional stick-drift challenges that often plague conventional analog sticks, and they provide long-term reliability especially for players who blueprint on spending 200 hours in GTA 6.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

They're also extremely customizable via the R5U's built-in Command screen, and are far more precise than analog sticks as they pick up even the most minute movements. Want to take out one particular NPC when they're surrounded by others in extremely close quarters? The R5U makes quick work of that. I've personally been alternating between my DualSense and the R5U for the best experience possible.

It has been revealed that there's so much to love about the Sony PlayStation Pulse Wireless Headset that I couldn't help but award it 4-stars in my review. Thanks to its planar drivers (developed in collaboration with Audeze) and Sony's amazing Tempest 3D Audio, the Pulse delivers a truly immersive gaming experience — especially in GTA 6 where it brings the chaotic and vibrant world to life.

With the Pulse's spatial audio capabilities, PS5 players can experience sounds from different directions and distances which makes it a walk in the park to stealthily walk around and past enemies. Not just that, but you can hear the rain like it's actually falling overhead, and idle chatter from NPCs swirls around your head as you change direction.

When it comes to combat and cop chases, the Pulse makes gunfire, explosions and footsteps sound life-like. Hearing sirens approaching from different directions makes you feel like you're actually Lucia or Jason. Aside from the phenomenal sound quality, the Pulse is extremely comfortable, and I haven't felt any discomfort even when I've worn the headset for six straight hours.

In a recent development, battery life is another major advantage, as the Pulse is rated for up to 30 hours between charges. No one's going to be playing for thirty consecutive hours but if you are (I know GTA 6 can be addicting), rest assured that you won't need to charge the headset for a while. I've been thoroughly enjoying using the Pulse to play GTA 6, and I don't see that changing anytime soon.

Sources indicate that I gave the SteelSeries Arctis Nova 5 a full 5-star rating because this headset is simply fantastic. Sleek, lightweight, and premium-looking, it's an excellent headset to use with an array of gaming devices. It’s extremely comfortable, boasts great sound quality, and the companion app lets you customize your gaming experience further.

SteelSeries Arctis Nova 5 (U.K.): was £129 now £79 @ Amazon.

Industry observers note that the Cherry XTRFY H3 is compatible with a plethora of consoles (except for Xbox) and it’s very comfortable for long periods of time. Fitted with 53mm dynamic drivers and utilizing spatial audio, it creates immersive soundscapes. The detachable mic cancels out background sounds, too.

Cherry XTRFY H3 (U.K.): was £84 now £64 @ Amazon.

The Logitech G325 Lightspeed is designed well and is extremely comfortable to wear for long periods of time, and it packs 24-hours of battery life. Thanks to multi-platform compatibility, it’s the only headset you need for a range of consoles and devices. In-game audio quality is fantastic as the treble and upper ranges are vibrant and sharp.

Logitech G325 Lightspeed (U.K.): was £69 now £59 @ Logitech.

Sources indicate that sony’s standard PS5 pad remains one of the best controllers around thanks to its responsive haptic feedback and adaptive triggers. Standard colourways, including white, midnight black, cosmic red, and galactic purple, are all discounted right now.

PlayStation DualSense (U.K.): was £64 now £42 @ Amazon.

According to recent reports, the Turtle Beach Victrix Pro BFG Reloaded improves on its predecessor by introducing Hall Effect thumbsticks and triggers with five stop switches. These are extremely responsive and so are the four on-the-fly customizable back buttons. The gamepad’s biggest selling point is its modular design and 11 interchangeable components which make it suitable for nearly every genre.

Turtle Beach Victrix Pro BFG Reloaded (U.K.): £174 @ Amazon.

In a recent development, the Razer Raiju V3 Pro's TMR sticks offer precise control over movements while removing the risk of stick drift, and the gamepad’s Hall Effect triggers are fantastic too. The controller is highly customizable with removable back buttons and personalization via Windows and/or mobile software, and it’s very comfortable for long gaming sessions.

Razer Raiju V3 Pro (U.K.): was £199 now £149 @ Amazon.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that even six decades into his Hollywood career, Steven Spielberg is still synonymous with a brand of movie magic and spectacle that very few can rival. And when he decides to direct a latest popcorn blockbuster like “Disclosure Day,” you know you’re in for a few dazzling sequences.

Industry observers note that one of the most exciting moments in the film comes when a train collides into a car with stars Josh O’Connor and Emily Blunt close at hand. The sequence tested every department, from camera and production design to visual effects. And during IndieWire’s recent Craft Roundtables, VFX Supervisor Matthew Butler explained the unique challenge of incorporating subtle VFX work into a scene where so much happens in camera. Related Stories If There’s Generative AI in ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth,’ It’s Not the First Time David Fincher’s Used It Trump Renews Backing for Federal Film Tax Credit as Lawmakers Push for Year-End Passage.

It has been revealed that “With Steven, he wants everything to be as practical as it can be,” Butler noted. “We had a real train. A real train, a real car attached to that train, it was being dragged on a real track. That actually did happen.”.

According to recent reports, but while Spielberg’s preferences were clear, Butler clarified that blockbusters on this scale rarely come down to a binary choice between practical effects and VFX. The biggest scenes often contain elements of both, as the pairing between in-camera human acting and cutting edge post-production is what leads to movie magic.

“When you combine some of the live action blue screen work, clearly that’s your lead actor and actress there, and your stunt work where it’s like ‘Oh my God, that looks really real’ and the stuff that you just can’t do that’s just too dangerous … that’s where visual effects came in,” he remarked. “But I wouldn’t say it was a visual effects sequence. It was a sequence that contained all of those, and it came together in the right way.”.

More coverage from IndieWire’s Craft Roundtables will be published here over the coming weeks.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that looks like Hollywood could be heading into the new year with relief on a national level.
  • “It’s running its way through Congress, and it has unbelievable support,” Trump said.
  • Sources indicate that trump mentioned Georgia and New Jersey by name as states with good tax credits for film and TV production, but argued that those incentives alone would not bring enough production work back from overseas.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that looks like Hollywood could be heading into the new year with relief on a national level. The push to pass a federal film and television tax credit by the end of 2026 picked up momentum on Friday at a White House press conference, where President Trump stated his administration was actively negotiating the measure and predicted it would pass.

“It’s running its way through Congress, and it has unbelievable support,” Trump said. He singled out Senator Adam Schiff, the California Democrat who introduced the bill with Republican Senator Tim Scott of South Carolina back in September, and said, “I tell you what, Adam Schiff said, ‘Wow, we love that bill.’ Adam Schiff said that.” Related Stories Box Office: ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Debuts to Mighty $120 Million, Reviving Lionsgate’s Most Important Franchise Box Office: A24’s ‘You Can See Everything’ Crosses $100 Million Globally.

Sources indicate that trump mentioned Georgia and New Jersey by name as states with good tax credits for film and TV production, but argued that those incentives alone would not bring enough production work back from overseas. With a federal credit, he stated, “Hollywood would open again.”.

It has been revealed that trump said his administration was also negotiating whether to extend the measure to benefit movie theaters, but said the matter was unsettled. He first publicly called for a federal production incentive in August after meeting with actor Jon Voight: one of three industry “special ambassadors” he appointed early last year.

The bill’s sponsors revealed more than 60 new House cosponsors and four new Senate cosponsors on Thursday morning — with lawmakers from both parties signing on in both chambers. The following day, Trump himself brought up the Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act in response to a question about whether he could work with Democrats. Calling the bill “very bipartisan,” he said, “I can tell you right now it’s going to happen.”.

Trump gave no timetable, though earlier this week, Representative Linda Sánchez, one of the bill’s House sponsors from California, called for Congress to pass it before 2027 so productions could qualify for benefits on the first of the year.

“Members of both parties have watched jobs in their districts move overseas,” she remarked in a release from Schiff’s office sent to the press. “Momentum is on our side, and we need to strike while the iron is hot by passing this bill before the end of the year.”.

Industry observers note that A floor vote has yet to be unveiled, but multiple sources told IndieWire the measure would move faster if attached to a stopgap government funding bill. If passed and approved, the federal initiative would give qualifying film and TV productions a 20 percent credit on labor expenses for American workers. The credit could reach 30 percent for productions that qualify for bonuses.

For crews accustomed to watching projects follow tax breaks to Canada or the U.K., the proposal would give producers a clear financial incentive to keep that work here for them in the U.S. The bill’s new Senate cosponsors include Republicans Katie Britt of Alabama and Thom Tillis of North Carolina — as well as Democrats Chris Coons of Delaware and Dick Durbin of Illinois.

The AFL-CIO and the American Hotel & Lodging Association also endorsed the bill, joining a coalition that already included IATSE, SAG-AFTRA, the Directors Guild of America, and the Motion Picture Association.

“Given the support from Republicans and Democrats in both chambers and the president, we can get this legislation across the finish line,” Schiff noted.

As most of the Marvel movies are now part of the multiverse, their franchises are all considered as one, the Marvel Cinematic Universe. While this list focuses on movie franchises, we also take into account major titles based on TV or games, but they have to have at least a sequel or two seasons. This list does not account for cameos as being part of a franchise. So, now, who are the actors with the most franchises?

It has been revealed that laurence Fishburne has amassed a variety of roles that stretch across sci-fi, superhero films, action movies, and even animation. Among the seven franchises he's in, he is notably most famous for The Matrix, playing the effortlessly cool mentor Morpheus. He reunites with Keanu Reeves years later when he joins the John Wick film series. He is also one of the actors who are in both the MCU and DCEU, having starred in Ant-Man and the Wasp and Man of Steel.

Recent findings suggest that fishburne's greatest strength in these franchises is the authority he brings to the screen. Even when he's not playing the lead, his characters tend to occupy positions of influence, making him a natural fit for franchise filmmaking. His deep voice and commanding presence are pivotal to his performance. His voice has made him join several franchises, including Transformers One and his first Marvel film, Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer. His franchise roles do not stop at movies, as he also stars in Hannibal and the upcoming season of The Witcher.

Pedro Pascal is having an exceptional run in his career. He shot to fame after his memorable turn in the fourth season of Game of Thrones as Oberyn Martell. At that point, Pascal had worked for at least fifteen years on TV. After Game of Thrones, Pascal joined the Star Wars universe as the titular character in The Mandalorian, then he joined the Kingsman franchise, the DCEU and MCU.

His seven franchise roles also include a villainous turn against Denzel Washington in The Equalizer 2 and the HBO hit series based on the best selling game, The Last of Us. Like Pattinson, fans have been saying that he's in literally everything. Just in the past five years, Pascal has starred in eleven feature films. What is great about Pascal is that he's able to balance his franchise commitments with exciting movies made by notable directors like Ari Aster and Celine Song. In a way, it is quite similar to how Pattinson operates these days. Pascal will next be seen in Avengers: Doomsday.

According to recent reports, harrison Ford is one of the most recognizable franchise actors in film history, having helped establish two of cinema's most enduring blockbuster properties. His most famous roles are Han Solo in Star Wars, appearing in the original trilogy and returning for the sequel trilogy, and Indiana Jones as the titular character, which spans five films. Most recently, Ford joined the Marvel Cinematic Universe as Thaddeus 'Thunderbolt' Ross, taking over the character in Captain America: Brave Latest World.

With a total of seven franchises in his filmography, he has become one of Hollywood's most bankable stars. In the 80s and 90s, he also starred in Blade Runner and Jack Ryan films, and he is still the definitive actor in both of those franchises. His other lesser known or less well-received franchises include the action stars reunion The Expendables and the animated film The Secret Life of Pets 2. Apart from his franchise films, Ford is also a reliable star in his own right, having starred in iconic movies such as The Fugitive and Witness, which earned him his sole Oscar-nominated role to date.

Recent findings suggest that four sides, four completely different answers to the same question about how a galaxy should work. Here is where you would have signed up, what it would ask of you, and what it would give you back.

You belong with the side that has almost nothing and keeps going anyway. The Rebellion is not a glamorous posting, and anybody who tells you otherwise has not seen what it actually costs the people inside it.

According to recent reports, you belong to the machine, and the uncomfortable truth is that the machine mostly runs on people who are competent, orderly and convinced they are doing their job properly. Very few of them think of themselves as villains.

In a recent development, ralph Fiennes has appeared in at least seven major franchises, often taking on some of their most influential characters. His most famous franchise role is undoubtedly Lord Voldemort in the Harry Potter series, where he portrayed the Dark Lord across four films. He later joined the James Bond franchise as M taking over the role from Judi Dench. He has also entered another major franchise with his portrayal of President Coriolanus Snow in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.

Just earlier this year, Fiennes turns in a stellar performance in the underrated 28 Years Later: The Bone Temple as Dr. Ian Kelson. His other notable franchise roles include Alfred in the Lego movies, Hades in Clash of the Titans, and a starring role in the Kingsman prequel, The King's Man. His career demonstrates an impressive ability to disappear in a role, completely shedding his famous personas like Voldemort for other roles. With years of experience tackling harrowing drama, romance, and blockbuster action, Fiennes is still a very much in-demand actor for Hollywood tentpoles and smaller indie dramas alike.

Industry observers note that dwayne Johnson has been on top of the highest paid actors in Hollywood five times and that is, in part, because of his franchise starring roles. His most prominent franchise appearances include Fast & Furious, where he plays the always sweaty Luke Hobbs and the Jumanji reboot trilogy. His first foray into acting was also in a franchise film, The Mummy Returns, which then spawned a spinoff franchise, The Scorpion King.

Johnson could have even more franchises, but unfortunately several titles that he tried to launch, such as Hercules and Baywatch, did not find their audiences. Nevertheless, he is still one of the most recognizable actors working in Hollywood today.

Hailing from Denmark, Mads Mikkelsen has built an impressive international career, moving seamlessly between European cinema and some of Hollywood's biggest franchises starring in eight. His first Hollywood franchise starring role was opposite Daniel Craig in Casino Royale, as Le Chiffre. That role seems to define him as Hollywood continues to cast him as an antagonist in other franchises, with the exception of Clash of the Titans and Rogue One.

His antagonist roles include Kaecillus in Doctor Strange, Grindelwald in Fantastic Beasts, and Dr. Voller in Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny. He also has made a lasting impression as Hannibal Lecter in the fan-favorite, cult show Hannibal. As a villain, Mikkelsen has never dialed his performance to an obvious level of evil, but instead he brings understated menace and nuance that makes his screen presence even more terrifying. Audiences who like his performances should also seek his "good guy" roles in movies such as Another Round or Polar.

Recent findings suggest that stellan Skarsgård has established himself as one of the most recognizable European actors working in Hollywood, with appearances in 8 major film and television franchises. His franchise experience also spans genres, from musicals like Mamma Mia to horror like the Exorcist prequel, making him a prolific performer who excels in any film.

Djimon Hounsou has built an impressive franchise resumé through appearances in some of Hollywood's biggest blockbuster properties, starring in at least nine so far. It has been revealed that samuel L. Jackson is arguably one of the most prolific franchise actors in Hollywood, having appeared in an extraordinary number of blockbuster films throughout his career. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Guardian reports that three US senators have sent letters to the CEOs of Apple, Google, and Meta, demanding answers about their failure to prevent access to AI-powered ‘nudify’ apps. Here are the details.

Last month, Apple updated its App Store rules in an attempt to crack down on apps that enable consumers to generate nonconsensual nude images.

According to the updated rules, apps that allow consumers to create AI-generated content must include safeguards against abuse, including tools to filter objectionable material, report offensive content, and block abusive users.

Apple also warns that apps used primarily for pornographic content or the objectification of real people may be removed from the App Store without notice.

While definitely well-intended, Apple’s changes came amid growing reports of AI-powered nudify apps, which easily allow users to generate nonconsensual intimate images.

Two months before these changes, Apple removed an app that allowed users to create pornographic deepfakes of real people after WIRED reached out for comment, which in turn came one month after San Francisco City Attorney David Chiu demanded that Apple and Google remove several nudify apps from their app stores.

Apple also removed several apps following investigations by the Tech Transparency Project (TTP), which published reports in January and April revealing that such apps were widely available on the App Store, sometimes even appearing in sponsored search results.

Throughout these investigations, Apple has maintained that nudify apps have always been prohibited under its App Review Guidelines, and that it proactively rejects and removes apps that violate its policies, including those flagged through user reports.

Apple, of course, is not alone in this challenge, with Google facing similar criticism over their availability on the Play Store, and Meta coming under scrutiny for allowing developers to advertise these apps on Facebook and Instagram, as highlighted in the WIRED report mentioned above.

Which brings us to today’s report from The Guardian.

According to The Guardian’s exclusive report, “three Senate Democrats sent letters to tech CEOs saying safeguards against nudification apps are insufficient on their platforms.”.

A trio of US Senators say Apple and Google are failing to effectively detect and remove apps that can be used to generate nonconsensual nude or pornographic imagery. They also say Meta is continuing to profit off of ads for these so-called nudification apps that “victimize women and girls worldwide”.

The senators, namely Ron Wyden of Oregon, Ed Markey of Massachusetts, and Ben Luján of Upcoming Mexico, claim that in addition to failing to remove these apps, the companies may actually be profiting from their distribution and promotion.

Commenting on the letter, both Google and Meta said they prohibit such apps or their promotion and work to detect and remove violations from their platforms, broadly echoing what Apple has repeatedly stated when reached for comment in the past over these same complications.

However, Wyden’s office argues that simply reaffirming, or in Apple’s case, updating these policies, means little if the companies continue to struggle to enforce them.

It has been revealed that keith Chu, the chief communications adviser and deputy policy director to Wyden, said that clarifying policies is not the same thing as enforcing them. Despite the companies reaffirming the prohibition of these apps, they continue to proliferate across Apple and Google app stores or be promoted in ads on Meta platforms, he added.

In its latest investigation, published just last month, TTP found 135 apps capable of generating nude or pornographic imagery on the App Store and the Play Store, using accounts registered to 13-year-old boys.

Additionally, researchers found that even accounts configured with parental controls were able to download these apps without requiring parental approval.

Despite Apple and Google removing the apps identified in the investigation, The Guardian noted that these apps continued to work on devices where they had already been installed.

Now, Senator Wyden warns that Congress may need to step in if the companies fail to do a better job of cracking down on these apps.

To read The Guardian’s full report, follow this link.

According to recent reports, update, 8:40 p.m. ET: In a statement to 9to5Mac, Apple stated:.

Recent findings suggest that “We designed the App Store to be a safe and trusted place for owners. A number of the apps in the TTP report are mainstream photo and video editing tools with legitimate, widely used functionality, and do not have nudification or deepfake capabilities. We prohibit nudify apps on the App Store, and remove developers who add capabilities like it after the App Review process — a malicious tactic known as bait-and-switch. We previously removed 28 of the apps referenced in this report before it was shared with us and have taken action on the remaining apps found to violate our rules. The report also relies on testing from older software that does not reflect current Apple safety features, including expanded protections for teens and parental controls in Screen Time that give families the ability to block kids and teens from downloading apps rated above their age.”.

Expanding on the safety features mentioned in its statement, Apple noted that teens aged 13 through 17 now have certain protections enabled by default, including web content filters, even if their parents haven’t configured any restrictions, and pointed to ⁠this support article for more information.

The manufacturer added that children under 13 are required to use Child Accounts, and that the report relied on its previous 17+ age rating system, which was replaced last year with a more granular system that includes 13+, 16+, and 18+ ratings.

Just curious. Why doesn't someone from Apple try out the app before approving it, rather than approving it and waiting until people complain? I know there are many thousands of apps on the App store. But given that Apple makes money off most of these apps, it could surely afford to hire a staff charged with reviewing submitted apps to ensure compliance with the App store's guidelines and requirements before making them available in the App store. What am I missing here?

Apple also noted that in its report, TTP counted apps depicting people in swimwear or lingerie, which the organization noted does not constitute nudification or, in itself, violate its guidelines.

As for parental controls, Apple explained that, although apps that exceed a child’s configured age restrictions won’t appear in curated App Store sections, they can still be found through search, allowing children to request permission to download them through Ask to Buy. Without parental approval, the download remains blocked.

In a recent development, apple added that Ask to Buy is supposed to require parental approval even for purchases made using gift card balances, including subscriptions. The company said that if a purchase didn’t trigger an approval request, that would be unexpected behavior, and that it is investigating further.

Recent findings suggest that update, November 19, 4:00 p.m. ET: In response to Apple’s statement, TTP director Katie Paul reached out to 9to5Mac with the following comment:.

According to recent reports, apple’s statement on nudify apps sidesteps key issues and leaves out key context. The company indicates it prohibits nudify apps but doesn’t address how its age rating system for apps contributes to the problem. TTP has shown how Apple relies on information provided by app developers to set age ratings—a self-reporting system that allows many nudify and pornographic apps to be misleadingly labeled a suitable for minors. Apple also continues to talk about removing nudify apps from the App Store, without mentioning that apps that are “removed” continue to be fully functional on people’s phones.

There are many questions about Apple’s policy on nudify apps that the statement fails to address. Apple has adopted a limited definition of “nudify.” The organization defines nudify apps as capable of showing someone naked, not stripping them down to a bikini or lingerie. But the company also indicates it bans “creepy” and “nonconsensual intimate imagery.” What if an app is used to depict a woman in a bikini without her consent? We have asked Apple to clarify that and have not heard back.

Recent findings suggest that as for Apple’s comment that TTP relied on “older software,” that may refer to the fact that Apple rolled out newly introduced child safety features in the fall. Our research was conducted in summer 2026. But many of Apple’s new features pertain to parent-supervised accounts on Apple, which have to be set up by a parent. Apple relies entirely on parents to go out of their way to locate and enable these settings. This raises obvious questions about how many people actually do this.
