Every Magic: The Gathering Power Nine Card, Ranked By Rarity

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1363 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Screenrant

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that if you've played Magic: The Gathering for a while, you've probably heard people mention "Power Nine" cards, especially the most infamous card in trading card game history, Black Lotus.
  • These cards are so strong that they were banned from most competitive MtG settings early on, and have become some of the most valuable cards ever created, particularly if you can get Alpha Edition versions.
  • Of course, in order to be able to play them in a Vintage format or casual game, you need to be able to own them first.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that if you've played Magic: The Gathering for a while, you've probably heard people mention "Power Nine" cards, especially the most infamous card in trading card game history, Black Lotus. The "Power Nine" are nine cards that were printed in the original MtG sets, starting in 1993, and are considered to be the most powerful cards in the game.

These cards are so strong that they were banned from most competitive MtG settings early on, and have become some of the most valuable cards ever created, particularly if you can get Alpha Edition versions. These days, some competitive formats will allow for these cards in rare situations, particularly the "Timetwister" card, or will let players use them in restricted ways in formats such as Vintage.

Of course, in order to be able to play them in a Vintage format or casual game, you need to be able to own them first. The rarity and notoriety of these cards mean that even later reprints of them don't come easily or cheaply.

Out of the nine cards in this list, five of them are the "mox" cards for each of the five colors in the game. A "mox" is a piece of jewelry that generally contains a gemstone that produces mana for its player.

Before restrictions were placed that would either ban the cards entirely or only allow for one per deck, players could play multiples of these cards in a single turn, which would give them an extremely powerful and unbalanced mana acceleration.

"Mox Emerald" is the green mana variety of these cards. Tapping the artifact could be played as an interrupt and adds one green mana to the player's mana pool. Alpha Editions of the card can run around $7,500 at the time of writing, according to TCGPlayer, with Unlimited Editions being priced closer to $3,000.

According to recent reports, "Mox Pearl" plays the same as its Emerald version, as do all the "mox" cards in this list. In this case, tapping the card will add one white mana to the player's mana pool.

Recent findings suggest that most competitive play formats have these cards Banned entirely, although Vintage format games will allow players to use them at a Restricted legality of only one per deck. This prevents players from having the overwhelming mana acceleration, at least a bit.

Due to its age, it's very hard to find an undamaged version of the original Alpha Edition card, so near mint listings are around $12,000 per TCGPlayer. Damaged versions can be much cheaper, as are later reprints such as the 30th Anniversary Edition, which is priced closer to $550.

As one can probably guess, "Mox Ruby" is the red mana variety of these "mox" cards and gives red decks a significant boost in mana acceleration. Like its companions, it is not Legal or is Banned in most competitive formats and Restricted in Vintage format games. Although, of course, with prior discussion and agreement, players can use them in casual games.

In a recent development, the original version of this Mono Artifact was part of the first 1993 MtG sets, and is difficult to come by in good condition these days. Finding a near mint version can cost upwards of $16,500 per TCGPlayer, with Collector's Editions of it running around $750.

According to recent reports, with artwork looking fairly similar to the "Mox Ruby" card, with a gemstone set in the middle of a gold necklace, the "Mox Jet" card once again follows the same ruleset. Tapping this card will add one black mana to the player's mana pool, and all of the "mox" cards come with the benefit of having a zero cost, making them even more impressive and dangerous.

Recent findings suggest that values of the "Mox Jet" card tend to bounce around quite a bit, with recent sales and listings according to TCGPlayer showing near mint varieties of the Alpha Edition coming in at around $16,500. Even the more recent Collector's Edition version of the card is inching towards four digits, with its average price currently being close to $900.

Next up we have one of the Power Nine cards which is not of the "mox" variety. This "Ancestral Recall" card adds quick card draw at low cost, giving players the ability to immediately draw three cards. Alternatively, they could force their opponent to draw three cards, but in a game where having the right cards in your hand can change your luck, most players would rather get the three cards themselves.

"Ancestral Recall" was also part of the original MtG set from August 1993, and is Restricted in Vintage formats while being Banned in all other official competitive play.

In a recent development, at the time of writing, TCGPlayer does not show any listings for the Alpha Edition card that are in better condition than heavily played, with even those cards coming in at prices around $10,000. Unlimited Edition versions are much more common and typically priced around $3,000 to $5,000.

The most valuable and rare "mox" card in the Power Nine collection is the Alpha Edition of "Mox Sapphire," which adds one blue mana to the player's mana pool.

Currently, TCGPlayer does not show any listings for the card that are better than moderately played condition, with even those cards being priced between $12,000 and $17,000. Unlimited Editions of the card average around $3,500 in value, although Collector's Editions are more reasonable at an average market price of $650.

It has been revealed that despite having some of the coolest art of the Power Nine cards, "Timetwister" was another 1993 card that was put on Restricted lists in 1994 and later Banned in most formats. However, this is the only Power Nine card that is presently Legal to play in Commander formats.

The card gave players the ability to shuffle their hand and draw another seven cards for a fresh hand at a low cost of only three mana. It is assumed that the decision to make it legal in Commander comes from the fact that not only does the card benefit the player, but it applies to all players.

Near mint versions of the card are priced at around $16,500 according to TCGPlayer.

It has been revealed that reading the ability of "Time Walk" makes it pretty clear why this card is considered overpowered. "Time Walk" costs only two mana and allows its player to take another turn with no limitations or drawbacks. Giving a second turn in a row at such a cheap mana cost can create wildly unbalanced games where opponents may not get to play much at all, particularly if its player has multiple copies.

Like the majority of Power Nine cards, it is Restricted in Vintage formats, and Banned everywhere else in competitive play. Although if you can convince someone to allow you to play with multiple copies in a casual game, it can be pretty fun. For you, at least.

Per TCGPlayer, Alpha Editions of the card in near mint condition can run around $22,500.

Easily the most infamous card in MtG, if not just in general amongst all trading card games, we conclude with "Black Lotus." This card is so well known that many people who have never even played the game are aware of its existence and value.

According to recent reports, the card costs nothing to play and allows players to sacrifice it to add three mana of any color to their pool immediately. If someone gets this card in their hand on turn one, it's entirely possible to win the game on the very first turn by casting a high-cost spell right out of the gate. Because it can add any color, it fits into nearly any deck and strategy with ease.

According to TCGPlayer, the card is valued at around $120,000 for near mint versions of the Alpha Edition. However, in the past, the card has sold at auction for upwards of $500,000.

So, even though it is possible to play as a Restricted card in Vintage formats, it's probably better to protect it from wear and tear in playing Magic: The Gathering.

It has been revealed that every once in a while, Instagram rolls out an upgrade that addresses one of its customers’ most longstanding requests. Today is one of those days.

As spotted by The Verge, Instagram head Adam Mosseri confirmed today that the app will finally let users edit a Story after publishing.

This means people will be able to add stickers and drawings, fix typos or adjust text, and even change the music without having to delete the Story and publish it again, which would mean losing any views it had already received.

The catch is that people will only have 15 minutes after publishing a Story to make changes by tapping the ellipsis button at the bottom of the screen, and then selecting “Edit story.”.

Here’s Mosseri’s post announcing the news:.

A post shared by Adam Mosseri (@mosseri).

Today’s patch is the latest in a series of changes Instagram has made this year to address longstanding user requests.

Recent findings suggest that back in March, the app introduced the ability to reorder photos and videos in a carousel after publishing. In April, it added an option to edit comments (also within 15 minutes of posting), and in June, it began letting consumers manually rearrange posts on their profile grid.

More recently, Instagram also brought its free Edits video editor to the Mac, with multi-track editing, advanced color grading tools, and 4K exports.

If There’s Generative AI in ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth,’ It’s Not the First Time David Fincher’s Used It

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the uproar over the alleged use of generative AI imagery in “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” has taken a familiar path.
  • Recent findings suggest that the criticism is of the use of generative AI in principle as a fundamental betrayal of the creative process — but it’s also of Fincher, as a director who, historically, has been meticulous with the level of detail and intention in every single shot of his films.
  • According to recent reports, at first blush, his approach seems at odds with using generative AI video, which relies on regurgitated (and, it bears repeating every time, stolen) data.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the uproar over the alleged use of generative AI imagery in “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” has taken a familiar path. Early responses to the Netflix film penned by Quentin Tarantino and directed by David Fincher have pointed out egregious examples of generative video artifacts sticking out in key flashback moments in the film — including one shot from the trailer where it certainly looks like a video AI program rendered a wagon the wrong way around.

Recent findings suggest that the criticism is of the use of generative AI in principle as a fundamental betrayal of the creative process — but it’s also of Fincher, as a director who, historically, has been meticulous with the level of detail and intention in every single shot of his films. In the early responses to Fincher’s latest, there’s been a lot of surprise and disappointment about this particular filmmaker being caught up in an AI controversy. Related Stories Trump Renews Backing for Federal Film Tax Credit as Lawmakers Push for Year-End Passage ‘Disclosure Day’ Did Its Biggest Stunts Practically, So the VFX Team Worked Hard to Look Invisible — Watch.

According to recent reports, at first blush, his approach seems at odds with using generative AI video, which relies on regurgitated (and, it bears repeating every time, stolen) data. But Fincher has defended his use of AI to the LA Times as a way to continue to innovate on an art form that is, after all, just over a hundred years old.

In a recent development, that defense really shouldn’t be surprising, given Fincher’s history with AI specifically. Although he’s been critical of generative tools in the past, Fincher admitted to using them (never publicly disclosing which) in the 4K remaster of “Se7en,” which the director described as a process of needing to remake the negative in order to battle the ravages of time (and the thousands of tiny scratches that would show up in 4K). “If you could see a 30-year-old negative and what it looks like even when immaculately stored — it was an enormous amount of fixing, just digs and scratches and cinch,” he told EW at the time.

That kind of image restoration technology was around long, long before the Anthropic IPO failed to save the stock market, but its level of precision has increased enormously in the past year. There were also sequences in the stored “Se7en,” though, where generative tech filled in gaps from the original. For one example, Fincher talked about a moment where a camera pan overshot the mark and changedh a shot. The performance had been good enough to use a technically flawed take — and, combined wit an unused take, allowed software to generate the missing information and restore the intended image.

Recent findings suggest that “It ends up being the most thrillingly stupid fix in the world because if you see it, we didn’t do our jobs. And you probably won’t see it. You probably won’t be aware that it’s happened. But you look at it, and you just think to yourself, ‘It’s so nice that we can fix that kind of stuff today,'” Fincher told Collider about that moment in “Se7en.”.

By Fincher’s own lights, then, the problem with AI in “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” is that people are painfully aware of it. AI critics might make a distinction between video restoration tools that work on existing projects and those tools being used because they can more quickly and cheaply generate originals that would’ve otherwise needed to be crafted by human hands. Having something AI-generated isn’t necessarily better than nothing when it comes to art, and choosing to AI-generate a Western chase sequence inside of, say, 10 seconds isn’t a solution to all.

Still, Fincher knows what he’s doing. This past week, he emphasized to the LA Times that he’s not a Luddite when it comes to film: “We’re talking about a thing that’s a hundred years old, and everyone’s going, ‘Stop. Pencils down. No more iterating. It’s not necessary to have at your fingertips the ability to change the color of that person’s eyes.’ Well, it exists. Should we not use it?”.

In a recent development, the answer is an emphatic “No!” to some And they can certainly be mad, or disappointed, or disheartened about Fincher’s decision to use AI tools. The one thing they shouldn’t be is surprised.

You may be tackling your hot sleeping problem by investing in a specialist cooling mattress, but it’s equally crucial to make sure the bed supports your sleep style and body weight (no back pain here, thank you.).

Generally, side sleepers benefit from beds on the softer end of the mattress firmness scale as more cushioning ensures their joints are cradled to avoid aches. Meanwhile, front and back sleepers need a firmer sleep surface to keep their hips aligned through the night, preventing back pain.

Sources indicate that body weight comes into it too. Firmer beds best support heavier bodies while lighter bodies would find these too harsh, needing a softer surface to sink into.

In fact, that’s another advantage when it comes to choosing to the Bear Elite Hybrid and Saatva Classic Mattresses — they both come in three firmness levels, from soft to medium and firm, to suit different bodies.

Other factors, like mobility and overnight company, can influence your mattress buying choices, too. People with reduced mobility may need a mattress with strong, sturdy edges they can push off from to get out of bed. Moreover, if you share a bed with a fidgety partner, you’ll want it to be good at absorbing motion so you can’t feel their movements from one side of the bed to the other.

Industry observers note that A lot of mattresses these days come with some form of cooling properties, so knowing your firmness, comfort, and support preferences can narrow down your search — with best prices swarming the whole market around Black Friday mattress shopping can be a minefield. The last thing you want is to tackle one sleep problem but trigger another.

You can invest in the coolest mattress on the market, but dress it incorrectly and it’s game over. For maximum cooling, look for a breathable mattress protector and moisture-wicking bedsheets that will accentuate heat dissipation rather than trap warmth.

In terms of sheets, the Sijo Airyweight Eucalyptus Sheet Set is our top pick for warm bodies. Made with Tencel fabric, these sheets absorb moisture while staying lightweight so you don’t wake up sweaty or clammy.

Hybrid mattress are generally cooler than memory foam mattresses, no matter how much cooling gel is infused in their foams. Hybrid mattresses, which feature pocketed coil layers alongside layers of foam and other materials, allow better air circulation as heat can escape out of the bottom and sides of the bed rather than pooling beneath you.

It has been revealed that on the other hand, foam layers tend to act like sponges, holding on to any heat your body gives off as you sleep. Yes, cooling infusions (like Phase Change Material, GlacioTex and copper) can help manage that heat to some extent. But, ultimately, hybrid beds will always be more breathable and reliably temperature neutral.

It has been revealed that so, you're probably wondering which hybrid mattress we recommend to hot sleepers. Sources indicate that also, let’s get this clear: cooling tends to mean temperature neutral, not actively refrigerating. Non-smart cooling mattresses generally use materials to help dissipate body heat rather than making the bed surface physically cold.

Sources indicate that that said, a smart air-or-water-based cooling mattress or mattress cover like the Eight Sleep Pod with automatic, responsive temperature controls can actively cool down your bed surface and adjust its temperature through the night in response to your fluctuations. And yes, it is as good as it sounds. If you’re seriously struggling with night sweats or hot flashes, and have a $2,600+ budget, we recommend investing.

Latest Update: Six Things You Should Do Now to Optimize Your Setup for GTA 6

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1139 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, you’re almost ready for Grand Theft Auto VI.
  • Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 is absurdly large.
  • Alternatively, it’s pretty easy to add more storage (if you can afford it).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, you’re almost ready for Grand Theft Auto VI. You’ve preloaded the game on your console, you’ve taken the next month off work, and you’ve locked your phone in a Faraday cage and set it adrift at sea. You’re prepared to lock in, and you haven’t forgotten a thing…right? Well, just to make sure, here are the most important tips to optimize your setup before you fire up the most anticipated game of the decade.

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 is absurdly large. According to Rockstar, you’ll need up to 212GB of storage space. For high-end consoles like the PS5 Pro, that’s more than 10% of the available storage space, and close to half the space on the more budget-conscious Xbox Series S. There’s a good chance you’ll have to delete something to make room.

Alternatively, it’s pretty easy to add more storage (if you can afford it). External SSDs are probably the cheapest route, though you’ll want to make sure to use a high-speed USB cable to connect it. It’s even worth shopping around for alternate models of SSD. For example, at the time of writing, the popular 2TB WD_BLACK external drive was close to $200, but the exact same drive in pink was $132.

You can also directly upgrade the storage of your console with expansion drives. The Xbox Series X|S supports proprietary expansion cards, while the PS5 and PS5 Pro can accept most M.2 internal SSDs. These will generally be faster, since they plug directly into the console via higher-speed connections than a drive hooked up via USB.

Let’s face it: Half the fun of any sandbox game is the weird, unique stuff that happens to only you. So you’re probably going to be hitting that “record recent gameplay” button more often than usual. While you’re cleaning up your storage space (or adding more), make sure to account for all the video clips you might want to save.

File size of video clips depends on a lot of factors, but 4K recordings can generally take up to 0.5GB per minute of footage. You can cut that down by saving footage in 1080p instead, but either way you’ll want to leave a little extra space.

Game footage is also a pretty good place to look if you need to make room on your console and don’t want to delete any games. Be honest with yourself: You don’t need all those clips from Horizon Forbidden West you saved four years ago. Dive into the settings on your console and find the biggest media files you forgot you even had on there.

Industry observers note that according to Rockstar, GTA 6 will be targeting 30fps across consoles at launch, which is pretty low as modern AAA games go. Part of the reason for that is all the processing power going to rendering a complex environment, but it also means you won’t need a fancy high frame rate TV or monitor any time soon to get the most out of it. Still, it couldn’t hurt to check a few settings on your display.

Industry observers note that first, make sure you’re using a higher refresh rate than 30Hz. While the game is targeting 30fps, it is technically capable of more, so if your console can keep up, you don’t want to accidentally bottleneck your frames. This setting will vary by device, so check the manual that came with your screen.

Also, make sure you have HDR enabled on your hardware. There’s a good chance this is already turned on for your TV, but sometimes other devices can switch display modes if they only support SDR. The game will help you calibrate your HDR settings for GTA 6 specifically when you launch it, but only if it detects HDR compatibility in the first place.

According to recent reports, if you’re planning to buy a console specifically for GTA 6, this might be one of those rare instances where a PS5 Pro really is worth the upgrade. According to Rockstar, certain features like ray-traced shadows will only be available on the Pro version of Sony’s console.

More importantly, the PS5 Pro version supports PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (or PSSR), which upscales lower-resolution images to get better detail and higher frame rates out of the same hardware. Given that GTA 6 is already starting at a meager target of 30fps on most consoles, anything that can give your frame rate a boost is probably going to feel like a welcome improvement over the baseline.

Recent findings suggest that I’ll tell you a secret as someone who’s spent a lot of time testing different game controllers: Most of the time, you really don’t need an expensive “elite” controller. Most of the time. I don’t buy into the idea that a taller control stick is going to make you an esports athlete. It can be nice to have, but it’s not a game changer. What does matter is customizing your controls, especially for long gaming sessions.

The DualSense Edge wireless controller is a favorite of mine, mainly because of the rear paddles and adjustable triggers. The former lets you map any button to a rear lever that you can access with your fingers underneath the controller, which can often ease some of the wrist strain of awkward button combos. And the adjustable triggers let you activate the buttons with less motion, again reducing repetitive stress.

The Xbox Elite Series 2 controller has similar features for the Xbox, as well as custom caps for the D-pad. Both consoles’ versions of pro controllers are more expensive than the standard ones, but if you’re planning to game for many hours, it can be worth it to get a controller that’s more comfortable for you.

If you have an Xbox One, you don’t necessarily have to upgrade your console to play GTA 6, but you might want to take a look at your network. GTA 6 will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming on day one, and you’ll be able to stream the game to an Xbox One console (as long as you purchase Cloud playtime as well or get some with your Game Pass subscription). This is the only way to play on a console older than the current generation, so if you don’t want to shell out for latest hardware, this might be your best bet.

According to recent reports, xbox recommends a minimum of a 20Mbps connection to run cloud gaming, but more is obviously better. If you can connect your console to a wired Ethernet connection, that would be better and provide more stability. If you can’t connect a cable, then at least make sure you’re well within range of your wifi router, and try to limit any other bandwidth-hogging applications on the network while you’re playing.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that in a new interview with Billboard’s On the Record with Kristin Robinson, Apple Music’s Zane Lowe discussed the early days of Apple Music Radio and revealed just how many people tune in each month.
  • Apple is rarely terribly specific about how many people use its services, including how many tune in to its radio stations.
  • In 2019, for instance, Eddy Cue said Beats 1 (now Apple Music 1) had ‘tens of millions of listeners,’ but Apple has rarely provided more specific figures since.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that in a new interview with Billboard’s On the Record with Kristin Robinson, Apple Music’s Zane Lowe discussed the early days of Apple Music Radio and revealed just how many people tune in each month. Here are the details.

Apple is rarely terribly specific about how many people use its services, including how many tune in to its radio stations.

In 2019, for instance, Eddy Cue said Beats 1 (now Apple Music 1) had ‘tens of millions of listeners,’ but Apple has rarely provided more specific figures since.

Apple Music’s Zane Lowe, however, has now offered a more concrete figure, revealing that the service reaches over 50 million unique listeners every month:.

In a recent development, we were never, you know, delusional enough to assume we were going to get a huge audience overnight. We’d have to build it like anyone else would have to build anything. But we’ve just got to a point in our 11 years on where we now, overall, reach over 50 million unique listeners a month, which is a really large number for us, and it’s growing exponentially and really fast.

The revelation came in a wide-ranging interview published today with Billboard’s On the Record with Kristin Robinson, where Lowe discussed Apple Music Radio’s early struggles, its approach to supporting emerging artists, and why human curation remains central to the service.

When discussing the early days at Apple Music, Lowe recalled:.

When we started the radio here, I didn’t have access or opportunity with a lot of the artists that I built relationships with from the BBC because we were unproven. And I came over here thinking, “Well, I’ve got Jimmy Iovine over here, and I’ve got Apple over here and I feel unstoppable, and who’s not going to want to come and launch this thing with us?” But it was kind of crickets… As upsetting as that was at the time, two good things came out of it. Number one, it snapped me back into the reality force field of building something from scratch. And number two, it made us focus really clearly and in a massive way on newly introduced and emerging artists.

He also mentioned some of the first artists Apple Music Radio supported, including Billie Eilish with “Ocean Eyes,” Khalid with American Teen, and Bryson Tiller with his first song.

At the time, Lowe noted, these artists were just getting started, and supporting emerging talent became a defining part of Apple Music Radio’s approach, one that continues to this day:.

It has been revealed that the really cool number is on our radio network. We played — this year alone — over 6,500 individual artists, which is not a commercial radio model. [Other radio networks’] playlists are very small, and the amount of plays is very great. Our playlist is gigantic. We play a lot of different artists, and over half of those 6,500 artists we’ve played in one year are new or emerging. So, think about 3,300 artists, roughly, getting played, who may be on their first song, their first EP, their first album…It’s proof of concept. It’s great.

Still on the subject of the early days at Apple Music, Lowe said “it was very clear [from the start] that that was very crucial to everybody who was responsible for bringing Apple Music to life,” adding that “serving artists and the artistic community in a way that is of most value and of most service” still drives “a lot of the decision-making” at the platform.

When the conversation turned to Apple Music’s recent rebranding, which introduced a new logo physically created using sound waves from a composition by Fred again.., Lowe said he couldn’t speak to the decisions behind it, but stressed the human element and the creative process that went into it:.

We could have created that in a way that could utilize all of the tech available. We could type that into a prompt. But at the end of the day, seeing how it’s made is so much more additionally inspiring than just seeing it. It speaks to, I think, what we try to do here, which is, we love the process of what we do, and the result is a byproduct of getting to do it and loving to do it.

The matter of algorithms also came up when Lowe discussed Apple Music’s approach to music discovery, with the executive emphasizing the importance of human curation over automated recommendations:.

In a recent development, well, we don’t want to say that too loudly, because someone could be like, “Wait a minute, we could cut costs here? Man, how did we not think of that!” Look, I mean, jokes aside, we’ve been incredibly fortunate, and I’ve been incredibly fortunate to take that step from the BBC into a company and to work with people that value exactly what it is you’re describing: this idea of place and this experience of sharing things with each other, and how meaningful it is when someone shares a record with you and it comes with context. It’s a gift….

Yellowstone was a huge hit throughout its five-season run, but even the biggest fans of Sheridan’s Neo-Western family saga could hardly have guessed how many subsequent small-screen projects the show would spawn. First, there were Yellowstone’s prequels, 1883 and 1923.

Sources indicate that then, there were the many unrelated Sheridan highlights, including the five-season crime drama Mayor of Kingstown, Landman, Tulsa King, its upcoming spinoff Frisco King, The Madison, Lioness, Lawman: Bass Reeves, and the upcoming third Yellowstone prequel, 1944. There’s also Yellowstone’s two sequels Marshals and Dutton Ranch, the latter of which is drawing attention back to Sheridan’s major-screen career with a season 2 plot that owes its inspiration to 2015’s Sicario.

Before Yellowstone, Sheridan was best known as the screenwriter behind a string of hit 2010s thrillers. Although Wind River and Hell or High Water, both of which Sheridan also directed, were critical hits, it was 2015’s drug trade thriller Sicario that really put his name on the map. Sicario’s story follows Emily Blunt’s FBI agent Kate Macer as she joins Benicio Del Toro’s assassin Alejandro Gillick and Josh Brolin’s CIA operative Matt Graver in taking on the Sonora drug cartel.

At least, that’s what Kate thinks the CIA is doing when the extragovernmental agency joins forces with her in Ciudad Juárez. Throughout the twisty, cynical story of Sicario, it becomes increasingly clear that no one is as innocent and well-intentioned as they seem, and the entire criminal enterprise is even more morally rotten than viewers assumed heading into the dark crime thriller.

This moral ambiguity is what marked Sicario out as Sheridan’s strongest screenplay, and his best movie to date. While Yellowstone ultimately valorized John Dutton despite his obvious, egregious flaws, Sicario truly doesn’t present any of its characters as heroes, and instead confronts viewers with the immense complexity and overwhelming moral mess of the international drug dealing business.

Compared to the simplistic macho posturing of many later Sheridan projects, Sicario marks the closest that the writer/ director came to capturing the profound thoughtfulness found in indicates like The Shield and The Wire. To make this achievement all the more impressive, it is crucial to note that the movie is no dull lecture on the complexity of cartels. Instead, Sicario masks its smart commentary amid brutal, fast action and a genuinely unpredictable, shocking plot.

Fortunately for fans of Sheridan’s TV work, Yellowstone’s stronger successor Dutton Ranch is now positioned, in season 2, to bring back Sicario’s best storyline. Season 2 pits Beth and Rip against drug cartels, just like the protagonists of Sheridan’s most uncontroversially acclaimed work to date, and Dutton Ranch’s cartel storyline can now prove that the show is Yellowstone’s perfect successor in the process.

It has been revealed that while CBS’s comparatively tame cop show Marshals saw Kayce switch sides to work for the police, Dutton Ranch brings Beth and Rip closer to direct rivalry with organized crime than ever before. As surprising as it might sound, considering how obviously corrupt the Duttons themselves were, drug cartels were only ever a distant threat in Yellowstone. Compared to rival ranches and private equity firms, local meth dealers ranked low on the list of the ranch-owning family’s enemies.

In a recent development, A lot of demonstrates that share Yellowstone’s focus on morally dubious criminal families, like the BBC’s recent critical hit This City Is Ours, explicitly center on the drug trade. However, the only time that drug trafficking was mentioned in Yellowstone’s run was when distant problems like cartel pressure and faraway human trafficking rings indirectly impinged on the family’s attempts to control their vast ranching empire.

In contrast, Dutton Ranch season 1 jumped headlong into the topic of drug cartels when the show revealed that Annette Bening’s formidable villain Beulah Jackson was involved in a complicated scheme to traffic fentanyl in the bellies of live cattle. To get the drugs across the country for a Mexican cartel, Beulah arranged to have her workers stitch the opioids into the animals before their cross-border relocation.

While this plot might sound more suited to From Dusk Til Dawn: The Series than a Yellowstone sequel, Dutton Ranch’s soapy style makes the storyline feel unexpectedly fitting. The show’s atmosphere is even closer to the melodrama of its inspirations, Dallas and Dynasty, than the more dour Yellowstone was, so the shocking plot didn’t feel entirely out of left field. What did feel shocking was season 1’s finale, “El Padrino,” setting up a perfect mirror of Sicario’s themes.

Image courtesy of MovieStillsDb.

Industry observers note that in the finale, Beth and Rip drag a confession out of Beulah, but their exposure of the fentanyl smuggling scheme results in the cartel boss Mariano Reyes, the titular El Padrino, kidnapping Beth and Rip’s adopted son Carter. Both Sicario and its 2018 sequel Sicario: Day of the Soldado feature kidnappings as prominent plot points, with the second movie even centering on the kidnapping of a cartel kingpin’s teenage child.

It has been revealed that this highlights just how much, despite the success of Marshals season 2 among viewers, Dutton Ranch feels much closer to Sheridan’s existing efforts than the glossy CBS procedural. Excitingly enough, Dutton Ranch season 2 isn’t Sheridan’s only upcoming project that will see the creator return to the world of drug cartels. There's also 2027’s star-studded upcoming action thriller movie F.A.S.T, which sees him finally return to the significant screen.

Sheridan penned the screenplay for director Ben Richardson’s F.A.S.T, which tells the story of Brandon Sklenar’s former special forces commando who is hired by the DEA to take on CIA-backed dealers in a small town. With a killer cast including LaKeith Stanfield, Sam Claflin, and Juliana Canfield, F.A.S.T will ensure that, alongside Dutton Ranch season 2, the themes of Sheridan’s Sicario will be explored in more depth in 2027.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, “You Can See Everything,” an unconventional documentary about Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes in exile, has crossed $100 million at the global box office. Its success extends a hot streak for A24, the indie studio behind last summer’s blockbuster “Backrooms” as well as arthouse hits such as “The Drama” and “Primetime.”.

In a recent development, “You Can See Everything” now ranks as the eighth-highest grossing non-music documentary, moving ahead of “Deep Sea 3D,” and the second-highest grossing non-music and non-nature documentary, behind Michael Moore’s “Fahrenheit 9/11.” It’s unlikely to surpass Moore’s anti-Bush jeremiad, which grossed an astonishing $222.4 million when it opened in the height of a fiercely contested presidential election. Related Stories If There’s Generative AI in ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth,’ It’s Not the First Time David Fincher’s Used It Trump Renews Backing for Federal Film Tax Credit as Lawmakers Push for Year-End Passage.

Those aren’t the only benchmarks with which to measure “You Can See Everything’s” impact. It is now the seventh-highest grossing film in the history of A24, coming in behind “Materialists,” which earned $105.6 million globally. On a domestic basis, “You Can See Everything” is A24’s third-highest grossing film, ranking just behind “Backrooms” ($197.5 million) and “Marty Supreme” ($96 million). It should easily surpass “Marty Supreme” and that film had Timothée Chalamet and a boatload of Oscar noms behind it.

Industry observers note that “You Can See Everything,” which is co-directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, earned $2.5 million this weekend to bring its domestic haul to $93.5 million after six weeks of release. Most of its earnings have been stateside. It’s currently playing in Australia, the U.K. and Scandinavia and the studio mentioned its international rollout will continue over the next several weeks.

Industry observers note that A24 is trying to keep the hits coming with “Club Kid.” Jordan Firstman’s look at a party promoter forced to grow up when he discovers he has a son, grossed $1.4 million on 229 screens in limited release this weekend. It has earned $3.4 million since it debuted three weeks ago. A24 bought the film out of Cannes for $17 million.

Recent findings suggest that black Friday is usually a great time to grab a latest e-reader, but the ongoing RAM crisis has made that a question mark this year: Amazon recently raised the prices of all its Kindles by around $50 and refreshed the entire lineup, which means your odds of grabbing one at a significant discount are low. But you aren't totally out of luck: If you haven't noticed, micro-e-readers—I'm talking credit card-sized, with screens that measure around four inches—are all the rage in 2026, and right now, you can pick up one of them for around $55.

Industry observers note that if you too can see the appeal of carrying all of your books with you on a device so small you'll forget it's even in your pocket, it's a great time to jump in: The recently released Xteink X4 Classic is currently 38% off for Black Friday, bringing it down to $54.87, a record-low price. Meanwhile, the smaller X3 is $55.72, or 19% off. Both are available in either "mist grey" or "space black." The discounts should last through the end of Cyber Monday on Nov. 30.

In a recent development, xteink is a Chinese startup that shook up the e-reading world last year with the launch of the X4, a super bare-bones device that made up for its lack of features and usability with a cheap sub-$70 price point. Since then, a huge online community of fans has formed, sharing tips on Reddit and even coming together to crowdsource an alternate operating system that fixed a lot of early problems. Xteink promptly followed up the X4 with a slate of other devices, including the 3.7-inch X3 and the X4 Pro, which adds a front light and touchscreen (at the cost of screen clarity and two physical buttons).

Sources indicate that the X4 Classic and the X3 improve on the original X4 with quality-of-life upgrades like a larger battery, relocated page-turn buttons, a real-time clock, and a tilt-to-turn-page feature. They're also lighter and thinner than the X4, though there is a trade-off involved: They drop the USB-C charging port in favor of magnetic pogo pins that require a separate adapter (included).

These upgrades also increased the cost: The X4 Classic typically retails for $89, $20 more than the discontinued X4 and only $10 less than the X4 Pro, while the X3 launched at $79. But right now, the X4 Classic is just under $55, or around 38% off, and the X3 is about a dollar more. Either is a great option for those who prioritize crisp, readable text above the conveniences of a built-in light or touchscreen, as those add extra layers between the inner screen and outer glass. It's also crucial to understand what you're getting into: These devices support only e-books without Digital Rights Management (DRM), which means you can't use it to read your existing library of Kindle books. On the plus side, there's no longer a need to worry about flashing newly introduced firmware if you don't want to, as the native version has been totally overhauled and is now one of your best options (though the new firmware, called "Licorice," isn't available on the X3 quite yet).

Industry News: 10 Greatest Mystery Shows With Detectives, Ranked

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Trying to solve riddles, decipher clues, and unweave a tangled web of subterfuge is exciting.
  • Among the host of mystery TV reveals, these stand out from the crowd.
  • Bringing an anthology structure to the detective game, HBO's True Detective offers something different with every season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Everybody loves a good mystery. Trying to solve riddles, decipher clues, and unweave a tangled web of subterfuge is exciting. Audiences sit on the edge of their seats, wondering if they were right, and if the detective on screen will come to the same conclusion they did. Shocks abound, and enigmas grow more profound as the series goes on.

Among the host of mystery TV reveals, these stand out from the crowd. Not only do they feature exciting plotlines that keep viewers hooked and coming back for more, but they have at their helm key figures, detectives that fans can rally behind. Whether they are practically perfect or tragically flawed, these main characters serve as both protagonist and guide to the curious circumstances that abound. Watching them solve the case is cathartic, as viewers can both identify with and sympathize for these brilliant icons.

Bringing an anthology structure to the detective game, HBO's True Detective offers something different with every season. Never staying in one locale or setting for too long, it always feels fresh and interesting for audiences who want variety. This kaleidoscopic array of talent ensures that True Detective has no bad episodes and there is always something interesting to take away from it.

With the limited time commitment required, True Detective has been able to host a whole roster of tremendous talent. The cast has included TV and movie titans such as Matthew McConaughey, Woody Harrelson, Vince Vaughn, Colin Farrell, Mahershala Ali, and Jodie Foster, who won an Emmy for her performance. Watching some of the industry's best talents try their hand at playing a detective is highly entertaining, and it makes True Detective a terrific watch for mystery aficionados.

Sources indicate that the Residence is a Netflix original miniseries starring Uzo Aduba as Detective Cordelia Cupp. Cupp is a focused and determined investigator who comes with a few quirks. Although she would rather be birdwatching, she undertakes an unusual murder case in one of the nation's most significant locations, the White House. With so many witnesses and suspects, Cupp must sort through a haze of facts, figures, and misinformation to get to the truth.

The Residence is a brilliant ensemble piece, but Aduba undoubtedly steals the show as Cupp. As the solid center of a swirling vortex of interpersonal drama and emotions, she stays level-headed and even-keeled during the stressful situation. The Residence has an interesting Upstairs, Downstairs feel and takes viewers inside a historic home that not many are privy to. With its snippet of suspense contained within a single season, The Residence makes for a perfect weekend binge, and it can easily be added to an already full watchlist.

Recent findings suggest that devotees of British murder mysteries should add Ludwig to their watchlist. The series stars David Mitchell as John Taylor, a man who enjoys creating puzzles as his alter ego, Ludwig. When John's identical twin brother, James, goes missing, he assumes his identity and his job as a Detective Chief Inspector. Luckily, John is able to use his unique way of thinking and fantastic memory recall to his advantage, and he helps solve murder cases that seem baffling to the rest of the crew.

Recent findings suggest that ludwig has several mysteries going on at once. Audiences will come for the interesting crime-of-the-week episodes, but they will stay for the overarching riddle of what happened to James. As John becomes more intertwined with the life his brother left behind, it will be interesting to see if he wants to return to his old way of living, or if he has become too attached to his fresh role and to his sister-in-law, Lucy (Anna Maxwell Martin).

In a recent development, there is so much excellence in Agatha Christie's Poirot that it is hard to know where to begin. It is a fabulously loyal adaptation of Christie's work. The dedication to her original vision is evident in everything from the wardrobe and sets to David Suchet's exemplary performance as the titular detective. It combines cozy mystery with legitimate suspense, and it ends with one of the most dramatic character arcs ever put on screen.

Suchet's depiction of Poirot remains influential and iconic. He managed to capture every detail of the famous Belgian sleuth, from the deep-seated mores to the more whimsical traits. With an impressive run of 13 seasons, Poirot features many cameos by well-known stars, and anybody who was anybody wanted a role on the show.

A great detective is really just a personality with a method attached, which is why we keep remaking the same four of them. Here is yours, what it says about you, and the case for them being the best in the business.

You let people think you are not a threat and then you simply never go away. Columbo is the only major detective show that tells you who did it in the first ten minutes, because the pleasure was never the puzzle, it was watching a rich man slowly realise he is in trouble.

You are the most interesting person in the room and you know exactly how to use it. Rian Johnson built Blanc as a gentleman detective who is also an outsider everywhere he goes, which lets him be charming at people who would never otherwise talk to him.

Recent findings suggest that everybody tells you everything, and you have never once asked them to. Jessica Fletcher is a crime novelist from a small town in Maine who is so warm and so obviously trustworthy that suspects confess to her essentially as a social courtesy.

You expect to be lied to and you are almost never disappointed. Chandler wrote Marlowe as a man with a rigid private code in a city that has none, which is why he takes the case, solves it, gets nothing out of it and takes the next one.

DCI John Luther (Idris Elba) is a highly intelligent person who has the ability to think like a killer. This makes him an efficient and effective investigator in Luther. However, being a bright, burning star comes at a cost, and his unorthodox tactics often ruffle the feathers of his colleagues. Luther is a must-watch for fans of mystery and police procedural shows. The series earned 11 Primetime Emmy nominations, and its curious cases and sordid psychopaths remain thrilling to watch.

Sources indicate that elba is superb as Luther. He brings a gravitational pull that viewers can easily attach to, and watching his character struggle with both internal and external challenges drives the series on. Luther was so popular that it got a spin-off movie in 2023 called Luther: The Fallen Sun. Elba's Luther makes for a captivating antihero, and watching him go toe-to-toe with serial killers is prestige TV at its finest.

According to recent reports, castle is a procedural mystery featuring a strong female lead. Stana Katic shines as Kate Beckett, a police detective who is haunted by her mother's unsolved murder. When bestselling fiction author Richard Castle (Nathan Fillion) is allowed to shadow Beckett as a muse for his newest series of novels, all sorts of exciting and comical situations abound. Castle and Beckett, or "Caskett," make for the perfect odd couple, and the growing romantic tension between them is palpable.

Castle is a wonderful suspense show because the type, severity, and intensity of the cases varies widely throughout the series. It is also a great detective feature because of Beckett. Driven by such personal motivations, she throws herself fully into her work and is determined to get the justice and closure she did not for other grieving families. Beckett is not afraid to stare evil in the face and then put the cuffs on it. Watching her work with the team and learn to trust Castle is a highly rewarding character journey. Her clever, no-nonsense approach is the antithesis of Castle's more hopeful and idealistic worldview. The writing adds plenty of levity, and Castle makes for a cozy whodunnit series that many can appreciate.

Sources indicate that A successful spin-off of the original Law & Order series, Law & Order: Special Victims Unit has recently reached a historic milestone in celebrating the debut of its 600th episode. One of the keys to its excellence is the perfect pairing of Detectives Olivia Benson (Mariska Hargitay) and Elliot Stabler (Christopher Meloni). Together, the two balance each other out, keep each other focused, and create the ideal team to tackle a bevy of criminal cases.

What makes SVU so rewarding to watch is the pursuit of justice. Sadly, many of the disturbing cases featured on the show are taken directly from real-life situations, and watching the despicable human beings get what they deserve is satisfying. Hargitay is riveting as Benson, and watching her do her thing makes SVU the epic TV drama that it is. SVU is the longest-running U.S. primetime live-action series for a reason, and when it comes to detectives that audiences both respect and adore, there are few better than Hargitay as Benson.

It has been revealed that updating the well-known fictional sleuth for the 21st century, Sherlock gives Sir Arthur Conan Doyle's beloved character a modern makeover. Incorporating technology into Sherlock's legendary methods of deduction is sublime, and it is fascinating to speculate on how he would interact with and feel about smartphones, the internet, and more. Each episode lasts around an hour and every minute feels warranted. Sherlock does a masterful job of taking the time and space to give layered mysteries satisfying conclusions and the elbow room to explore more of Holmes' personality.

In a recent development, sherlock Holmes has been depicted many times on the small and large screen, and Benedict Cumberbatch's portrayal is one of the best. Cumberbatch captures the restless ennui of being smarter than everyone around him and craving mental stimulation in a world that rarely affords it at the level he needs. Despite Sherlock's obvious disdain for sentimentality, there are several moments in the series where the curtain is pulled back a bit, and viewers get to see him in vignettes of vulnerability. Sherlock is an incredible series and undoubtedly one of the best to have been released within the past few decades.

A TV series doesn't win 20 Emmys for being mediocre, and the groundbreaking NYPD Blue is anything but. Created by Steven Bochco and David Milch, NYPD Blue revolutionized the cop procedural. Gritty, realistic, messy, and colored in shades of gray, it drew outside the lines and challenged the cut-and-dry politics of earlier cop dramas. The main characters were flawed and complex. They didn't always make the right choices, and their ethics and personas were multidimensional.

Recent findings suggest that NYPD Blue has a fantastic cast of actors including Dennis Franz, Kim Delaney, Jimmy Smits, and Esai Morales. No matter if their tenure lasted a few seasons or the entire series, each actor brought their respective role to life in brilliant form, and audiences were hooked. It might be easy to take NYPD Blue for granted now, but it was unlike anything seen on TV when it debuted, and its impact can be felt in every police drama that has followed.

Sources indicate that when the phrase "TV detective" is brought up, one character chiefly comes to mind. The disheveled hair, the gravelly voice, the long trench coat evoking memories of 1940s gumshoes. We are talking, of course, about Lt. Frank Columbo. Brought to life by the indelible Peter Falk, Columbo is the hallmark of television sleuths.

Recent findings suggest that the classic TV show was unique in that instead of primarily focusing on the "who," Columbo was equally interested in the "how." Although Columbo is smart and works out theories in his mind, it is his unassuming charm and patient demeanor that disarms suspects. As Sherlock Holmes is a savant of clues and facts, Columbo is a master of human behavior. He understands people inside and out and uses this to his advantage, anticipating how they would think in a given situation and what they are likely to do.

Sources indicate that like a Komodo dragon waiting days for its prey to die, Columbo never rushes at anything. His quiet tenacity plays the long game. He can't be unnerved, and that scares the daylights out of criminals. Watching fiends who think they are more clever than anyone else and are used to manipulating people get outwitted by a cigar-smoking, quiet-voiced, middle-aged man with messy hair is endlessly satisfying. Columbo remains the best TV detective show, and it is no mystery as to why.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the Harry Potter TV show has faced a lot of backlash before it even comes out, with the latest one related to the Elder Wand, but it’s missing the point. The trend of remakes and reboots is still going strong in both film and TV, and in the latter, it has been most frequent in the fantasy genre. Worlds like those of The Lord of the Rings and Percy Jackson have found fresh life with TV highlights, and now the Harry Potter franchise is joining the fun.

Instead of exploring other stories from the Wizarding World, the Harry Potter TV show is a new adaptation of the books, with the first season, titled Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone, covering the first novel. The Harry Potter TV show features a new cast of new talents and well-known actors, with the plan being that every season will cover one of the novels, and the show has already been renewed for a second season.

It has been revealed that as mentioned above, the Harry Potter TV show has already faced backlash for different reasons – many aren’t on board with a upcoming adaptation, others didn’t like the casting choices, and others are skeptical. The latest target is the Elder Wand, shown in a character poster starring Dumbledore (John Lithgow), and which is being criticized for its design – but all this backlash is missing the point of this specific wand.

As season 1 of the Harry Potter TV remake adapts the first book in the series, it will explore Harry’s (Dominic McLaughlin) life with the Dursleys, how he learned the truth about his parents and that he’s a wizard, his arrival at Hogwarts, his meeting his new best friends Ron (Alastair Stout) and Hermione (Arabella Stanton), and his first encounter with the dark side of the wizarding world. The trailers and teasers for HBO’s Harry Potter adaptation have already given the audience a taste of its visual style and more, and the character posters give a closer look at some details.

The character poster for Dumbledore features the famous wizard with his wand, the legendary Elder Wand, one of the Deathly Hallows supposedly made by Death. The Elder Wand is said to have been the most powerful wand in the wizarding world, and its core had the tail hair of a Thestral, which made it powerful but tricky to master. Dumbledore became its master after defeating Grindelwald, and it was one of the objects Voldemort was looking to obtain.

The Harry Potter movies made the Elder Wand one of the most beautiful wands in the wizarding world, with a design that made it stand out from other wands. Because of this, there has been a strong reaction towards the much simpler Elder Wand in the Harry Potter TV show, which looks like a regular wand. The latest Elder Wand is being called “boring” and “cheap” on social media, but the truth is that this new design is a lot closer to how the wand is described in the books.

It has been revealed that the design of the Elder Wand in the Harry Potter movies is iconic and beautiful, but it’s not an accurate design. In the books, the Elder Wand is described as coming from an elder tree on the banks of the river, with Death making “a wand from a branch that hung there”, which he later gave to Antioch Peverell, the older brother from the Tale of the Three Brothers. This implies that the Elder Wand had a very simple design, just like in the TV show.

Sources indicate that the newly introduced Elder Wand might not please fans of the Harry Potter movies, but those familiar with the books will surely be more open to it, as they know how it was described. The Elder Wand’s simpler design is actually good news, as it further reveals HBO’s commitment to staying as true to the novels as possible, even if that means being very different from the movies.

The design of the Elder Wand is just one example of many other details in the Harry Potter TV show that are more book-accurate than they were in the movies, which makes the project even more exciting, and it’s to be seen how well received they are by fans of the novels.

“The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” made quick work of the competition, debuting to an impressive $120 million and easily capturing the top spot on the domestic box office chart.

In a recent development, the sequel represents a massive improvement on the opening of its predecessor, 2023’s “The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes,” which bowed with $44 million, a franchise low. However, “Sunrise on the Reaping” can’t match the highs of the series. Its opening pales in comparison to 2013’s “Catching Fire” ($158 million debut), 2012’s OG “Hunger Games” ($152.5 million), and 2014’s “Mockingjay Part 1” ($121.8 million debut). Deadline trumpted the fact that the film has the second highest-grossing opening for a prequel behind “Rogue One,” which seems like a milestone no one really ever thought or cared about before. So extra credit to some enterprising studio publicist or Google for unearthing that gem. Recent findings suggest that but whatever records it holds, “Sunrise on the Reaping” has revived a series that was looking a little long in the tooth. Why did this “Hunger Games” outpace “The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes”? It probably helped that franchise icons Jennifer Lawrence, Josh Hutcherson, and Woody Harrelson were coaxed back for brief appearances. There was also a top-shelf cast that included Oscar-winner Kieran Culkin, Oscar nominees Glenn Close, Elle Fanning, Ralph Fiennes, and Jesse Plemons, and rising stars like Iris Apatow, Ben Wang, and Joseph Zada. Internationally, “Sunrise on the Reaping” earned $105 million from 84 territories, pushing its worldwide box office gross to $225 million.

Industry observers note that lionsgate is distributing the $150 million production, as it has the previous films. The studio has mounted something of a comeback under Adam Fogelson, who replaced Joe Drake as the motion picture chief in 2024. Lionsgate was on its back foot at the time, having released flops like “Borderlands” and the reboot of “The Crow.” In recent months, it’s fortunes have shifted thanks to blockbusters like “Michael” and hits such as “The Housemaid” and “The Long Walk.” A revived “Hunger Games” franchise is critical, as it gives Lionsgate another pillar for its slate.

But “The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes” success threatened to overshadow “I Play Rocky.” The Amazon MGM Studios release earned $9.3 million after expanding from 29 locations to 2,477 theaters. It’s playing like gangbusters, earning an A+ CinemaScore, a rare distinction that puts in the company of “Top Gun: Maverick” and “The Avengers.” The word-of-mouth is clearly excellent, which could help it build momentum over the holidays. It’s also worth noting that “I Play Rocky” is catering to older moviegoers who take their time getting around to seeing things. Even if it starts to fade, “I Play Rocky” is a relatively economical bet. It cost in the $30 million range to produce and has earned $10.4 million since it debuted.

Then there’s “Ebenezer.” The Johnny Depp revival isn’t as glorious as his most diehard fans may have hoped. The Christmas story fell roughly 60 percent in its second weekend, earning $7.7 million to bring its domestic total to $32.5 million. But Paramount didn’t spend lavishly to make the film. It only cost $38 million to remind Depp’s Scrooge of the Christmas spirit. “Ebenezer” has also earned $45.9 million internationally, bringing its global total to a respectable $78.4 million.

Among the newcomers, Sumerian Pictures released “Josephine,” a family drama with Gemma Chan and Channing Tatum,” on four screens in New York and Los Angeles this weekend, grossing an estimated $84,200 for a per-screen average of $21,050. The film earned raves at Sundance where it premiered and Sumerian bought it. “Elsinore,” a drama about Ian Charleson’s final stage performance, opened with $240,000 from six locations in New York and Los Angeles for a per-theater average of $40,000. Focus Features is distributing the film, which has earned Oscar buzz for Andrew Scott. Lastly, Janus Films and Criterion debuted Paul Thomas Anderson’s concert film “Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall” in three locations, where it earned $162,000 for $54,000 per-screen average. The film is only being shown in 35mm, which limits the number of screenings available to cinephiles and PTA completists.

For a mattress to be considered a good option for anyone with back pain, it needs to perform well in three specific areas; pressure relief, temperature regulation, and edge support.

Pressure relief score (out of 5).

In a recent development, temperature regulation: Reliable temperature regulation is an key feature of a mattress for back pain. Waking up hot and sweaty can lead to more movement (like kicking off the covers), which can cause further injury. Pressure relief: This is a term to describe how much cushioning there is along the touch points of the mattress. For example, for side sleepers, this will be your shoulders, hips and knees. For back sleepers, this will likely be your lumbar region and upper back and shoulders. Minimal pressure relief can lead to a build-up of pressure, which can exacerbate existing pain. Edge Support: This describes how sturdy a mattress is at its edges and corners. This is an important feature for any mattress, but especially those with back pain who may need to sit comfortably and safely before standing.

It has been revealed that cher Thompson is a Senior Staff Writer at Screen Rant, where she covers everything from explosive reality TV moments to cast interviews about the twists and turns of scripted dramas. With a background in creative writing, marketing, and teaching, Cher knows how to spot both the storytelling genius and the guilty pleasures in pop culture. Her work blends wit with insight, making readers feel like they’re chatting with a friend who just happens to know way too much about TV.

For years, Gilmore Girls fans have been in agreement about the final season of the series being the worst by far, and in a newly introduced documentary, the show's stars are finally addressing what led to the massive dip in quality.

Sources indicate that drink Coffee, Talk Fast: A Documentary About Gilmore Girls revisits the history of the long-running series, which began its run on The WB in 2000 and ended on the newly revamped network, The CW, in 2007. Several people involved with the series, including Kelly Bishop, who played Emily Gilmore, Michael Winters, who played Taylor Doose, and director Jamie Babbit shared their recollections of what took place after Gilmore Girls creator Amy Sherman-Palladino departed from the series, ahead of its difficult seventh season.

In a recent development, noted to be the show's weakest, Gilmore Girls season 7 often felt like an off-brand version of the hit's past life. While Sherman-Palldino and her creative partner husband, Daniel Palladino, weren't the only writers on Gilmore Girls, they brought a unique style to the series that the next showrunner, producer Phil Rosenthal, struggled to bring to the series.

Bishop offered a more reserved point of view, explaining that "it just wasn’t as strong a season, and that’s because [Sherman-Palladino] wasn’t there," but Babbit and others made it clear that it felt that there was a distinct lack of care that the show's original creator had brought to the series.

Sherman-Palladino's sometimes complex vision for Gilmore Girls, which was known for its fast-talking scenes that involved one steady shot and could take dozens of takes to get right, didn't make the cut when she departed the series. "The mandate was, ‘We don’t care if it’s good or not. We just want to go home...anything complicated was out the window," Babbit revealed.

In a recent development, according to Babbit, Sherman-Palladino's departure and changes to who was running the show were at fault for the quality dip of Gilmore Girls season 7. Rosenthal, a longtime producer of the series, came into the leadership role, but Babbit shared the higher ups "gave the leadership of the show over to the actors" who had spent years with grueling schedules that extended well beyond what had been scheduled. "The actors said, ‘Look, the thing that’s most important to us is going home on time.’".

It has been revealed that while Babbit and others were interviewed to lay out an oral history of the series for Drink Coffee, Talk Fast, it's not a surprise to viewers of the long-running series to learn that there was a far different energy at play throughout the run of the show's final season. Gilmore Girls, which returned with Sherman-Palladino's original vision for the show's end with a Netflix revival in 2016, was ultimately able to come to a less hotly-debated conclusion.

Industry observers note that 2025 saw the debut of Prime Video's Countdown, a highly entertaining, action-packed thriller series starring Jensen Ackles and Eric Dane with a unique premise that made every episode a must-watch experience. Unfortunately, despite a solid first season that culminated in a shocking ending, Countdown didn't get renewed, ultimately making it a one-and-done series. The show's appearance in Prime Video's global Top 10 rankings last November, following its cancellation, only proves that Countdown was a good show that deserved a better fate.

Industry observers note that countdown's one and only season opens with the mysterious murder of a DHS agent, which prompts FBI Special Agent Nathan Blythe (the late great Eric Dane) to form an elite task force composed of different branches of law enforcement, including LAPD Detective Mark Meachum (Ackles) and DEA Agent Amber Oliveras (Jessica Camacho), to get to the bottom of the murder. Task Force Hurricane eventually uncovers a plot perpetuated by the disenfranchised former Russian soldier Anton Volchek (Bogdan Yasinski) to construct and detonate nuclear weapons in the middle of Los Angeles. Every episode becomes a pulse-pounding race against the clock to discover Volchek's whereabouts and the nuclear bombs, with thousands of lives hanging in the balance.

However, Season 1's nuclear bomb threat is only part of the story. At the outset, it appeared that Countdown's main mission would have a season-long arc, similar to most action-thriller reveals on streaming. In Episode 10, however, the Volchek plot is completely resolved, with the show then embracing a 10-month time jump that results in a completely new storyline. Here, Agent Blythe reassembles his elite task force, this time named Task Force Armor, to investigate a conspiracy to assassinate a presidential candidate and the current POTUS. Countdown's approach proved unique for a streaming show, with a totally new conflict beginning in the latter four episodes, but the show's bold narrative attempt may have been too unique for its own good.

In a recent development, countdown's first season concludes with a heart-pounding cliffhanger in which the suspect behind the assassination plot, nicknamed "Todd" (Grant Harvey) by Meachum, is revealed to be an FBI agent. Initially, Task Force Armor appeared to be investigating an ultra-right-wing, anti-government fanatic, but revelations in the final episode suggest a deeper ulterior motive, with Todd leading the task force astray at every step of their investigation.

The episode that would turn out to be the show's season finale, "Your People Are in Danger," ends on a cliffhanger that makes the show's cancellation even more frustrating, as Todd takes Agent Oliveras captive and prepares to execute her, as he had done to his wife's pet dog in an earlier episode. The finale then cuts to the credits before Todd presumably opens fire. However, series creator and showrunner Derek Haas, via Bluesky, later revealed that Agent Oliveras was intended to survive past what ended up becoming the series' final moment.

According to recent reports, countdown was a solid series, headlined by the exceptional trio of Dane, Ackles, and Camacho. Ackles plays his character with tremendous pathos, as the series eventually reveals that Meachum has been diagnosed with a terminal illness and his symptoms are growing more severe. As the investigation into Volchek progresses, Meachum grows more reckless in the field, believing he must stop Volchek while possibly sacrificing himself in the process.

In a recent development, with its premise and format, Countdown felt closer to a spiritual successor of the iconic action-thriller series 24. Each episode featured an exciting action set-piece, raising the stakes and suspense while gradually peeling back the layers of the story's major antagonist. It was an exciting, unique series that Prime Video should have valued more. Despite a terrific cast, premise, and hook for Season 2, fans never learned Todd's true motives or identity, and the brewing romance between Meachum and Oliveras was never resolved. Nevertheless, viewers can decide for themselves by watching Countdown's existing episodes on the streamer.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Humanity has 400 years to prepare for an alien invasion in Netflix's 3 Body Problem, but fans have already spent nearly three of those years waiting for another season. Created by David Benioff, D.B. Weiss, and Alexander Woo, the Sci-Fi series arrived in March 2024 with a mystery involving disappearing scientists, impossible technology, and an enemy that won't reach Earth for centuries. Netflix has since confirmed that the story will continue through a third and final season, giving the creators time to finish adapting Liu Cixin's bestselling trilogy. Unfortunately, viewers hoping for an extra-long second season might be a little disappointed.

Netflix has officially confirmed that 3 Body Problem Season 2 will consist of six hour-long episodes, down from the eight episodes that made up Season 1. Season 2 will see humanity preparing for the San-Ti's arrival, both on Earth and in space. A fleet sets off on a mission that will take centuries to complete, while a secret hidden inside one man's mind could be humanity's best chance of surviving the invasion. And what's more, the show's creators have warned fans that if you thought Season 1 was mental, just wait:.

Recent findings suggest that “The story gets really wild in the best possible way. With something that’s that wild, there are a lot of choices to be made and a lot of things to be figured out. We’ve been putting our heads together to figure them out recently especially the past couple of months.”.

Recent findings suggest that benioff and Weiss have brought in two of their most trusted collaborators to see them through the season, as well. Jeremy Podeswa (Game of Thrones) directs Episodes 1–3, while Miguel Sapochnik (House of the Dragon) handles Episodes 4–6.

The cast stars Jess Hong (Inked) as Jin Cheng, Benedict Wong (Doctor Strange) as Da Shi, Eiza González (Baby Driver) as Auggie Salazar, Jovan Adepo (Watchmen) as Saul Durand, Liam Cunningham (Game of Thrones) as Thomas Wade, and Marlo Kelly (Dare Me) as Tatiana Haas. Fresh cast members include Claudia Doumit (The Boys) and Ellie de Lange (Wolf Hall), while Alfie Allen (Game of Thrones) will appear as a guest star.

Industry observers note that 3 Body Problem Season 2 premieres January 14, 2027, exclusively on Netflix. Season 1 is available to stream now. Stay tuned to Collider for all the latest news and updates on the biggest and best movies and highlights heading to your favorite streaming platforms soon.
